jobs.description:
Established in 2004, OLIVER is the world's first and only specialist in designing, building, and running bespoke in-house agencies and marketing ecosystems for brands. We partner with over 300 clients in 40+ countries and counting. Our unique model drives creativity and efficiency, allowing us to deliver tailored solutions that resonate deeply with audiences. 

As a part of The Brandtech Group, we're at the forefront of leveraging cutting-edge AI technology to revolutionise how we create and deliver work. Our AI solutions enhance efficiency, spark creativity, and drive insightful decision-making, empowering our teams to produce innovative and impactful results. 

Role: Senior Social Designer - 12 month fixed term contract

Location: London, United Kingdom

About the role: 

This is a senior, hands-on design role in a high-volume social studio, working on the account for one of our brand new FMCG clients. You'll be responsible for the quality and consistency of visual output across always-on and campaign work — balancing strong creative thinking with efficient delivery. You'll also help build the design infrastructure that allows the team to produce, adapt, and localise content at scale.

Success in this role looks like consistently high-quality visual work delivered at pace, clear improvement driven by performance insight, and a design system that makes the whole studio more effective.

As Senior Social Designer, you'll drive the visual craft of the studio — translating ideas into platform-native assets that are engaging, on-brand, and built to perform. You'll work hands-on across static, motion, and short-form video design, while building scalable systems that enable high-quality output to travel efficiently across markets. Based in London on a hybrid basis (2–3 days per week), you'll collaborate closely with Content Creators, Strategists, Social Media Managers, and the Social Creator Lead.

We support flexible working and are open to different arrangements. We offer reasonable adjustments throughout the recruitment process.

What you will be doing: 

  • Social-First Design Execution
    • Create high-quality visual content across static assets, motion graphics, and short-form video design support — including titles, overlays, and transitions
    • Ensure all design work is platform-optimised for TikTok, Instagram, YouTube Shorts, and other relevant channels — on-brand, consistent, and ready to publish
    • Maintain strong visual craft standards across every output, regardless of volume or turnaround time
  • Content Creation Support at Scale
    • Work closely with Content Creators to bring concepts to life visually and enhance content through considered design
    • Produce assets at pace across always-on content, campaign activations, and reactive or trending content opportunities
  • Scalable Design Systems
    • Create and maintain templates, layout systems, and modular design assets that enable content to be adapted quickly, localised across markets, and repurposed across formats
    • Document design systems clearly so they can be used consistently across the team
  • Multi-Market Adaptation
    • Adapt visual content for different markets, ensuring visual consistency, cultural relevance, and formatting and language accuracy
    • Support efficient versioning of assets across markets and platforms, setting clear standards for how adaptation is approached
  • Performance-Driven Design
    • Work with Data and Social teams to understand which visual approaches perform best, and use engagement signals to inform layout, format, and creative decisions
    • Continuously refine design approaches based on what the data shows — iterating quickly and sharing insight with the wider team
  • Collaboration and Workflow
    • Partner closely with the Social Creator Lead, Content Creators, Strategists, and Social Media Managers to ensure all work aligns with strategy, meets deadlines, and passes brand, legal, and compliance approval processes
    • Communicate proactively on timelines, asset status, and any risks to delivery
  • Creative Quality and Standards
    • Uphold high visual standards across all content formats, campaigns, and markets
    • Stay current on platform design trends, social creative best practice, and emerging visual formats — applying relevant insight to day-to-day output and sharing with the team
  • Budget and Production Management
    • Manage project-level production budgets including cost estimation, purchase orders, invoicing, and reconciliation
    • Source and negotiate rates with freelancers and production partners as needed, driving cost efficiency without compromising quality
    • Flag budget risks early and escalate where required

What you need to be great in this role: 

  • Strong design capability across static and motion formats, with a portfolio demonstrating high-quality social-first work
  • Proficiency with Adobe Creative Suite (Photoshop, Illustrator, After Effects, Premiere Pro), CapCut, Canva, Figma, or equivalent tools
  • Deep understanding of platform design best practices and what drives visual engagement across key social channels
  • Demonstrated ability to manage multiple design projects simultaneously, delivering consistently strong work at pace and under time pressure
  • Experience building and maintaining design systems, templates, and modular asset libraries that enable efficient, high-volume production
  • Background in high-volume, always-on content environments — agency, in-house, or embedded studio
  • Experience delivering social design for consumer brands, with FMCG background an advantage
  • Familiarity with multi-stakeholder environments involving strategy, social, data, and client teams
  • Experience managing project-level production budgets, including cost estimation, supplier negotiation, purchase orders, and reconciliation
  • Advanced use of Gen AI tools relevant to social design — including tools that support ideation, asset generation, content variation, and production workflow optimisation
  • Experience designing AI-assisted workflows for personal use and sharing effective approaches with the wider team
  • Ability to train others on responsible and effective use of AI tools within a design context
  • Agentic thinking for complex, multi-step design and production challenges — breaking problems down systematically and driving efficient execution
  • Strong understanding of AI capabilities and limitations, with rigorous human oversight applied to all AI-assisted outputs
  • Experience working across multiple markets or languages, or in embedded in-house or studio environments
  • Familiarity with paid social design requirements — safe zones, format variants, and performance testing
  • Experience designing for creator or influencer-led content
  • Experience building design systems or localisation frameworks at studio level
  • Formal qualifications are welcome but not required. Equivalent experience counts, whether gained through work, study, volunteering, or self-directed learning.

Our Global Structure


Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we're unlocking new possibilities as one global team.

We're looking for a Staff Product Manager in London to own major parts of that platform. Your customers are the engineers and ML researchers across all three brands who build AI products and agents. You'll work with engineering and product leaders in Europe and the US, and your decisions will shape how AI gets built across every market we operate in.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Set the strategy and roadmap for core parts of our GenAI platform: model access and routing, agent infrastructure, and evaluation and observability.
  • Build one platform for three brands. Spot the patterns across Deliveroo, Wolt and DoorDash teams and turn them into shared building blocks, so a capability built once reaches every market.
  • Shape our model portfolio across frontier and open-weight models. Decide where we build, buy or partner in an ecosystem that changes month to month.
  • Make agents production-ready. Give teams safe access to company knowledge, tools and systems, with the quality, latency and cost controls needed to run agents at scale.
  • Own the evaluation strategy so teams can prove quality before launch and keep improving it after.
  • Stay close to your customers. Work with the teams shipping AI experiences, measure adoption and time-to-production, and let real production use drive the roadmap.
  • Lead at a senior level,  presenting to senior technical leadership and influence strategy beyond your own roadmap.

What You'll Need to Thrive

Our ideal candidate brings deep expertise in some of these areas and curiosity to grow in others:

  • Significant product management experience (typically 8+ years, or equivalent), including owning a technical platform, developer product, or ML or data infrastructure.
  • Hands-on experience with LLM-based products or platforms in production, such as assistants, agents, evaluation or inference. GenAI platforms are a young field, so we care more about depth than years.
  • A platform mindset. You notice the problem five teams keep solving and turn it into one capability everyone can use.
  • The ability to go deep with engineers and ML researchers, then explain the trade-off in plain language to a senior leader.
  • A track record of leading large, ambiguous areas on your own and aligning stakeholders across companies, countries and time zones.
  • Comfort with regular overlap with US time zones, including some late-afternoon and evening calls.

What Success Looks Like

A team in any of our three brands can go from idea to a reliable AI product dramatically faster. That happens because the hard parts (models, inference, evaluation, tooling, observability, governance and agent infrastructure) are solved once at the platform layer and get better for everyone.

Why Join Us?

  • Real scale from day one. Your platform powers AI used by millions of consumers, merchants and couriers across three brands.

As a central point of coordination for Swiss site matters, you will help teams resolve operational issues, improve ways of working and ensure corporate services meet the needs of the business.

Corporate governance and administration

Policies, compliance and internal controls

jobs.title: 3D Computer Vision Research Engineer - World Map
jobs.description:
About Niantic Spatial

AI has learned from almost everything online, but it still struggles with the physical world, where 99.5% of economic activity happens. It doesn’t know where things are, how spaces fit together, or what changes over time.

That’s one of the biggest unsolved problems in AI, and it’s the one we’re solving at Niantic Spatial. We build spatial AI models and services so people and machines can reason, learn and act safely in the physical world. We turn camera imagery, video, sensor data and archives into accurate, AI-readable representations of real places that robots can train in and machines can use to know exactly where they are.

In physical AI, mistakes have real consequences. That’s why we build AI grounded in measured reality, not guesswork, so the people and machines relying on it can trust it to get things right.

Our team built some of the world’s most widely used maps. Now we’re building something bigger: a living, measured record of the real world that machines can query, learn from and use to understand how places change over time. If you want to help AI understand the world we actually live in, come build with us.

About the Role

You'll help build the geometric foundation of the next-generation world map — joining our World Map Research Engineering team (Geospatial Alignment) as a Research Engineer or Senior Research Engineer. This is an end-to-end applied research role that spans from strong engineering and data-systems work to R&D in 3D deep learning, transformers, and foundation models. You'll develop new algorithms, produce the research data and evaluation assets needed to advance them, and engineer the resulting capabilities into dependable production systems.

The World Map team works with heterogeneous captures from phones and handheld devices, aerial imagery, LiDAR, and 360 cameras, as well as external geographic and elevation data. The central challenge is to harmonize these data sources, quantify uncertainty, and maintain consistency as the map evolves.

You'll work at the intersection of cutting-edge research and scalable engineering — developing new approaches to geospatial registration, correspondence, and geometric optimization, then productionizing these technologies to directly improve Niantic Spatial's world model.

What You'll Do

  • Geospatial Registration — Develop and advance algorithms for world-scale georeferencing and registration across imagery, 3D reconstructions, point clouds, and geographic reference data.

  • 3D Geometry & Correspondence — Build and improve methods spanning multi-view geometry, SfM, SLAM, feature matching, learned correspondence, bundle adjustment, point-cloud registration, and ICP.

  • Data & Evaluation — Create the data and evaluation flywheel for world-scale mapping — design and maintain large-scale datasets, pipelines, benchmarks, and evaluation methodologies that expose hard failure modes, accelerate research iteration, and support production.

  • Learning-Based 3D Reasoning — Explore and develop learning-based approaches for geospatial understanding, combining transformers and 3D foundation models with geometric priors and uncertainty modeling.

  • Production Robustness — Design robust solutions for challenging real-world conditions: sparse or noisy GPS, changing appearance, inconsistent reconstruction quality, large geographic extents, and imperfect reference maps.

  • Cross-Functional Collaboration — Partner with leading researchers in visual localization, 3D computer vision, and mapping — as well as engineering and product teams — to identify high-impact problems and turn research breakthroughs into end-to-end production systems.

  • Research Communication — Share results clearly through technical writing, design reviews, and internal presentations; contribute to publications and open research where appropriate.

What You'll Bring

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Robotics, Machine Learning, Photogrammetry, or a closely related field — or equivalent research or industry experience.

  • Strong grounding in 3D computer vision, machine learning, robotics, photogrammetry, or a closely related area.

  • Demonstrated experience with 3D geometry and several relevant areas — multi-view reconstruction, SfM, SLAM, camera pose estimation, point-cloud registration, image-based localization, georeferencing, or sensor fusion.

  • The ability to formulate ambiguous real-world problems, choose the right mathematical or learning-based tools, and evaluate solutions rigorously.

  • Strong Python skills and experience with modern ML and scientific-computing libraries (PyTorch, NumPy, SciPy).

  • Strong software engineering skills — you can turn research prototypes into reliable, scalable, and maintainable systems.

  • A track record of taking an algorithm from research idea and experimental prototype through evaluation, benchmarking, and deployment on real-world data.

  • Clear written and verbal communication; able to collaborate effectively across research and engineering disciplines.

Nice to Have

  • PhD in computer vision, robotics, machine learning, photogrammetry, geodesy, remote sensing, or a related field — not required, but valued.

  • A strong publication record or active involvement in the research community at venues such as CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, NeurIPS, ICLR, SIGGRAPH, 3DV, ICRA, or RSS.

  • Experience with learning-based approaches for visual or 3D understanding — transformers, point transformers, foundation models, or methods combining learned representations with explicit geometric priors.

  • Experience with aerial or satellite imagery, GNSS/GPS, geodesy, mapping systems, or large-scale spatial data.

  • Evidence of technical leadership, mentorship, or successful cross-functional delivery.

Compensation & Benefits

Base salary: Competitive market rate. Compensation also includes an annual bonus, equity, and a comprehensive benefits package.

Location & Work Model

jobs.description:
About CircuitHub

CircuitHub is reshaping electronics manufacturing with The Grid, a factory-scale robotics platform that makes small-batch, high-mix electronics assembly radically more efficient. Think semiconductor-fab precision applied to the chaotic world of prototyping and low-volume production: a 10x throughput improvement in one of the world's most foundational industries.

We've raised $45M from top-tier investors including Plural, Y Combinator and Google Ventures, and we're already profitable. Our customers include a major EV maker, a top AI lab and many of the worlds largest companies.

The Grid isn't a prototype. It's live, scaling fast and delivering real revenue, and we're building the team that will scale it further.

The Role

CircuitHub makes electronics on demand. Engineers upload a circuit board design; we buy the parts, build the board in our own robotic factory and ship it. More and more of that business is now run by AI agents, and we want you to help build them.

These aren't chatbots. Our agents have real jobs:

  • They inspect boards. An agent checks camera images of every panel we build for wrong, rotated or missing parts.

  • They program robots. Agents read datasheets so our pick-and-place machines know how to handle each new part.

  • They watch the factory. They spot stray parts in robot storage, diagnose printer faults and clear stuck machines.

  • They run the back office. They book supplier invoices, chase late orders, explain quotes and triage bugs.

  • They write our code. Most of what our team ships starts in an agent session.

What you'll do

Find a process people still do by hand and automate it end to end: decide what needs judgement and what needs plain code, build the tools, and prove it works before it runs alone. Then make it cheaper, faster and right more often. You'll also improve the platform every agent runs on, and work closely with the people your work serves, from factory operators to finance.

How we build

  • Evals first. An agent earns the right to work alone: blind tests against people's verdicts, shadow runs beside the humans, replays of past decisions. We track accuracy and cost per run, and re-test whenever we change a model, a prompt or the effort level.

  • Agents judge, code writes. Agents return structured answers. Plain code checks them against a second source and makes every change.

  • Classical first, model second. Cheap vision and maths narrow the problem so the model only looks where it matters.

  • Safe by construction. Agents work in sandboxed cloud machines that never hold real credentials, and tool calls are built so a business action can't run twice.

Recent work

  • Image alignment ranks the parts on each board photo. The worst 20% of parts hold about 90% of real defects, so the agent only inspects those. In a blind re-run it caught all 13 defects operators had marked.

  • A photo check for stray parts in robot storage scored 10 out of 10 blind, at about 8¢ a photo. The model it replaced caught about half.

  • Agent tool calls leave durable receipts, so a session killed mid-deploy resumes without sending the same email or order twice.

  • Invoices extracted from supplier emails matched what a person had entered 66 times out of 66.

  • A constraint solver replans the whole factory every two minutes, across robots, ovens and people.

What we look for

  • You've put LLM agents into production and can tell us what broke and how you knew it was working.

  • You're a strong software engineer first. Most of this job is real engineering, not prompting: concurrency, idempotency, data modelling, security.

  • You build the eval before you trust the result.

  • You like the physical world: cameras, robots, parts rotated by 90°.

  • Bonus: computer vision, optimisation or electronics.

Stack

  • Agents: Claude Code, Codex, Claude and OpenAI APIs, MCP, skills in plain Markdown

  • Code: TypeScript (Bun, React), Python (FastAPI, Dagster, OpenCV, OR-Tools), PostgreSQL

  • Infra: Nix and NixOS, Nomad, Terraform, Vault, AWS, Modal sandboxes, OpenTelemetry

jobs.title: Member of Scientific Staff, Cell Culture and Functional Assays
jobs.description:
LOCATION: King's Cross, London · PATTERN: Lab-based, full-time

The opportunity

We're a stealth startup in AI and bio, building infrastructure for data generation. The team is small and elite, the problems are hard, and the foundations are being laid right now. You'd help write them from the first line, with real ownership and a direct line to the founders.

This role covers the cell side of our protein characterisation work. You would keep the cell lines healthy and run the assays that show how a designed protein behaves on a living cell, week after week, to the same standard.

About us

AI for biology has a data problem. The data that matters most doesn't exist yet, so we're building the infrastructure to produce it, with quality and traceability built in from day one.

We're in stealth and heads-down on execution. We'll share more about what we're building once you've spoken with the team.

The role

You will run cell culture and the cell-based assays for our protein characterisation work. That means the mammalian lines the assays depend on, from thaw through routine passage to a banked and documented stock, and the weekly rhythm of seeding, treating, reading and reporting plates.

Most of it runs in 384-well plates with imaging-based or flow cytometry readouts. You will run those assays as designed, with the controls and replicates that make a curve defensible, and you will be the person who notices when a plate, a line or a reagent lot has started to drift.

Assay design and the shape of the cascade sit with the scientist who leads this work today, so you are not being asked to invent the panel. You are being asked to make it run the same way every week, to record what you did in a form the rest of the system can read, and to tighten the protocols as they settle, including moving them towards the plate formats our automation will take on.

Your first 90 days

FIRST 30 DAYS

◆ Take over routine culture and banking for the protein cell lines, working to the protocols we already run.

◆ Learn the panel end to end by running each assay alongside the scientist who owns it.

DAYS 30 TO 60

◆ Run at least one assay in the panel independently, including its controls and acceptance criteria.

◆ Revise one culture or assay protocol so that someone else could follow it without asking you.

DAYS 60 TO 90

◆ Hold the weekly assay schedule on your own and return results on the agreed turnaround.

◆ Bring one protocol to a tighter precision bar, or into a plate format ready for automation.

Who you are

You are a hands-on cell biologist who takes assay variability personally. You have run the same assay often enough to tell a real effect from a bad plate, and you would rather find the cause than repeat the run.

The week has a rhythm in this job: cells to feed, plates to seed, runs to finish, numbers to return. You are happy with that, you keep records someone else can pick up, and you say early when something looks wrong rather than at the end of the week.

We do not hire people into boxes. The team is small, and early hires here end up owning work beyond the job they joined for. Nobody arrives with every part of this role. If you are strong in most of it and quick to learn the rest, we want to hear from you.

MUST HAVE

◆ Strong hands-on mammalian cell culture: adherent and suspension lines, aseptic technique, and thawing, passaging and banking to a high and consistent standard.

◆ Experience running cell-based assays end to end, including relevant controls, replicates and dose-response curves behind a reported number.

◆ Comfort with plate-based work and the arithmetic that goes with it, such as dilution series, plate maps and normalisation.

◆ Careful, traceable record-keeping that someone else can follow without asking you.

◆ A PhD in cell biology, pharmacology, immunology or a related field, or an MSc and two to three years of relevant lab experience.

NICE TO HAVE

◆ Reporter cell line bioassays for binding or blockade.

◆ Receptor internalisation, lysosomal trafficking or cytotoxicity assays.

◆ High-content or fluorescence imaging, and the image analysis behind it.

◆ 384-well formats, liquid handlers or other plate-based automation.

◆ Flow cytometry, for example for surface receptor quantification.

Why this is unusual

Most cell-based assay roles sit inside a discovery project. You build an assay, you answer a question with it, and the assay goes quiet. This one is closer to running an instrument. The same assays run every week against a stream of new molecules, and the number that comes out is the product.

That changes what good looks like. Precision matters more than novelty, a protocol is only finished when someone else can run it and get your answer, and every passage, plate and reagent lot is captured as structured data, because a result is only as trustworthy as the cells behind it.

Some people find that energising; some find it outside their lane. Worth knowing in advance which one you are.

How we work

This is a lab-based role at our site in King's Cross, London. The cells are in the lab, so most of your week will be too, with room for writing and analysis away from the bench. The wider team is distributed and travels, so you will work with people who are not always in the building.

We work in the open. Decisions are written down, work happens centrally rather than scattered across tools, and the week opens with a session the whole company attends. There is a quarterly offsite. Each person owns their area and makes the call inside it, and we will expect that of you early rather than late.

UK benefits are 30 days of annual leave plus public holidays, a pension with a 10% employer contribution, and top-tier Bupa private health cover. More is added as the team grows.

The team you will join

You will join the protein characterisation team and report to its lead. Day to day you will work with the scientist who designs the assay cascade, with the protein production and molecular characterisation scientists upstream of you, with the functional genomics team who share the cell culture suite, and with the engineers building the software and automation the lab runs on.

We are a small, elite team, and this is the first seat given entirely to the cell-based side of the work.

Our process

Our process has four stages. A short screening call about the role and the practicalities. A behavioural interview about how you work, run from the same template for every candidate, before anything technical. A technical stage with the protein characterisation team, built around real work rather than a puzzle, including time with us in person at the lab. Then references, aimed at whatever we still want to understand.

If you are not sure whether you match every line above, apply anyway. We would rather read it and decide.

We are an equal opportunity employer. We make hiring decisions on merit, scope-fit, and the strength of the working relationship we expect to build with each hire. Applications welcome from candidates of any background.

◆ Revise one protocol, including how its failures are captured.

thawing, passaging and banking, and transient transfection of HEK293 or CHO cells for expression.

NICE TO HAVE

◆ Cell-based assays such as reporter bioassays for binding or blockade, receptor internalisation or cytotoxicity, with imaging or flow cytometry readouts.

jobs.description:
Accreditation Manager

Build the processes that let Calibre expand into its next standard - and make every launch

easier than the last.

London, Aldgate East | 5 days in office | Start ASAP

£40,000-£60,000 + 0.1%-0.3% equity | 2-5 years' experience

Build a new kind of certification company

AI is changing how companies work. They still need independent assurance that their systems can be trusted.

Calibre is building a global certification business for that world, combining rigorous assessment with AI-powered operations.

Founded by two former Palantir engineers and backed by a $3.3m pre-seed round, we are starting with information security and expanding into AI management systems and further ISO standards. You will work directly with the founders to build the policies, processes and evidence that make that expansion possible.

What you will own

You will be the hands-on execution owner for new accreditation programmes, with an initial focus on ISO 42001 and expansion into other ISO standards. Gautham, CEO will manage you, and you will report directly to the founders.

- Write the substance. Translate standards and accreditation requirements into clear policies, procedures, responsibilities and records that reflect how Calibre actually operates.

- Find gaps and close them. Run and coordinate internal audits of Calibre's own systems, with appropriate independence and technical support. Identify missing evidence, test whether processes work, and build or improve them when they do not.

- Carry the accreditation process through. Maintain the requirements map and evidence trail; coordinate specialists, accreditation bodies and assessments; track findings, corrective actions and deadlines through to closure.

- Make the work compound. Turn each programme into reusable templates, clause mappings, evidence libraries, AI workflows and quality checks. Improve these with every assessment, then apply them to the next standard.

Support will be provided by our founders, technical specialists and commercial team, with commercial handoffs where needed. You will own making the work happen and ensuring it stands up to scrutiny.

What success looks like

A working set of internal processes that gives us confidence the next standard will be faster to add than the last: clearer requirements, stronger evidence, less repeated work and fewer avoidable gaps, while preserving the rigour of each assessment.

Rigour. Ownership. Good judgment with AI.

Who we are looking for

- 2-5 years of experience in consulting, clinical trials or medical device certification processes. You have learned to navigate complex requirements, demanding reviews and work where details matter.

- Strong writing and structured thinking. You can turn an ambiguous requirement into a precise policy, a workable process and evidence that it is being followed. You can explain and defend what you have written.

- A record of getting things finished. You have personally delivered complex work, coordinated stakeholders and resolved gaps. You follow up, raise blockers early and create a process when one is missing.

- Practical AI fluency. You are comfortable working with Codex, Claude Code or equivalent agents on substantive tasks and building reusable workflows around them.

Knowing when to stop using AI is essential

We want someone who knows where AI helps, how to give it useful context and how to verify its work against the source. Just as importantly, you must recognise when it is adding noise, missing the point or weakening the writing - and stop using it, think the problem through and write the answer yourself. You remain accountable for every output.

Experience with ISO management systems, internal audits, accreditation assessments, external assessors or workflow automation would be useful. Deep knowledge of every standard is not expected; the ability to learn carefully and execute is.

Why join Calibre

- Work directly with the founders on a central part of the business, with substantial ownership and visible impact.

- Build capability that lasts. Your policies and workflows will become the foundation for expansion across standards, with scope to grow as the business grows.

- £40,000-£60,000 salary and 0.1%-0.3% equity.

- 22 days of annual leave plus bank holidays.

We work together in our Aldgate East, London office five days a week. We are looking for someone who can start as soon as possible. Candidates must already have the right to work in the UK; this role does not offer visa sponsorship.

You'll sit at the intersection of commercial, product, and market expertise. You'll be the internal and external authority on Fuel Oil: responsible for the health, growth, and strategic development of the vertical, while acting as a key face to clients on complex and technical engagements.

You'll need to be equally comfortable deep in the market microstructure of Fuel Oil — cash differentials, arbitrage dynamics, blend economics, price relationships across bunkering, power generation and feedstocks — as you are presenting to senior client stakeholders, shaping the product roadmap, being the market authority on the most opaque part of the oil barrel, and harnessing the power of AI to turn your knowledge into the next generation of advanced tools for fuel oil trading.

  • Define and prioritise the Fuel Oil product roadmap with the product and technology teams

  • Act as the primary subject matter expert for all Fuel Oil decisions across the business

Building tools, models and AI agents (~25% of role)

  • Design and build Sparta’s next generation of heavy products analytical tools and pricing models

  • Own the fuel oil knowledge base behind our AI products: write the domain rules, test answers against desk judgement and catch errors before clients do

  • Prototype quickly with AI coding tools, then work with engineering to ship the ideas that work

Client interactions and technical demos (~15% of role)

  • Lead complex, discovery-focused and technical client conversations and demos

  • Support sales and account management on senior or strategically important Fuel Oil and Feedstocks opportunities

  • Represent Sparta at industry events, conferences and client visits as a Fuel Oil and Feedstocks expert

Market commentary and content (~15% of role)

  • Take editorial ownership of Fuel Oil market commentary and content

  • Define the voice and analytical framework for Fuel Oil commentary across client-facing and marketing channels

  • Work with analysts and contributors to keep output accurate, well argued and commercially relevant

Process and data quality (~10% of role)

  • Oversee the operational processes behind the vertical: cash differential modelling and uploads, component premiums and landed diffs, new arbitrage routes and price points, blend hub coverage, and ongoing data quality

  • Build scalable processes and delegate or automate routine tasks where it makes sense

Required

  • Deep Fuel Oil & Feedstocks market expertise — strong working knowledge of fuel oil benchmarks, differentials, blending economics, arbitrage mechanics, refinery economics, and global heavy products flows.

  • Proven experience in a commodity-facing role within energy trading, data/analytics, financial services, or a closely related field

  • Hands-on building experience: working knowledge of Python and SQL (or equivalent) and a track record of tools or models other people actually use

  • Practical experience with AI tools such as LLMs, coding assistants or agents, and good judgement about where they get the market wrong

  • Ability to turn market complexity into clear product requirements, specifications engineers can build from, and client value propositions

  • Confident and credible in client-facing settings, including technical discovery calls and senior stakeholder presentations

  • Strong written and verbal communication, with experience producing or overseeing market commentary

  • Comfortable working across sales, product, technology and research teams

Desirable

  • Experience with pricing, data, or analytics platforms in the energy space

  • Familiarity with fuel oil data operations: cash differentials, landed diffs and price curve maintenance

  • Experience shipping work to production alongside an engineering team (version control, code review)

  • Existing network within the Fuel Oil & Feedstocks trading community

What success looks like

In your first six months, you will have:

  • Taken full ownership of the Fuel Oil vertical and its operational processes

  • Established yourself as the go-to internal and external authority on Fuel Oil and Feedstocks

  • Shipped at least one new tool, model or AI capability that clients or internal teams use

  • Measurably improved the quality of our AI products' fuel oil answers, checked against desk review

  • Built strong working relationships with the content team and begun shaping commentary output

  • Led technical client engagements independently

Why Join Sparta?

At Sparta, our culture is built on innovation, collaboration, and high performance. We thrive in a fast-paced environment where initiative is celebrated, challenges are embraced, and impact is rewarded.

• Equity in a high-growth, VC-backed company

• $42M in Series B funding — strong market traction and investment

• Early-stage growth — build your career as we scale

• Market-leading product — we are redefining commodity trading intelligence

• Top-tier tools and technology to support your success

What's the Culture Like at Sparta?

At Sparta, our culture isn't just a set of values on a wall — it's how we work. We embrace a dynamic environment where initiative is celebrated, challenges are met head-on, and innovation thrives. You'll collaborate with people who are passionate about our mission and committed to building outstanding products and outcomes for our customers.

The Sparta Code

Understanding is non-negotiable

Understanding leads to believing. Believing leads to winning.

The 'why' is the difference between compliance and conviction. Before we execute, we ask: why does this matter, who does it serve, what changes if we win? People who understand the mission don't need to be managed.

Ask for forgiveness, not for permission

Most decisions are reversible. Most fears are not.

The mission wins. Your idea doesn't have to.

Conflict is a gift

Honesty is an expression of care.

We Are Sparta

Sparta is the AI leader for commodity trading, home to Leonidas AI, the first operating system for oil and commodity traders.

Backed by $42 million in Series B funding led by One Peak, with participation from returning investors FirstMark and Singular, the same investors behind AI leaders like Legora, Dataiku, and Synthesia. Most companies are building a chatbot on top of data. We've built an agent with an actual reasoning layer, grounded in years of proprietary market data and in-house trading expertise nobody else has.

We're scaling fast, and it's an exciting time to join. From independents to multinationals, the world's leading commodity teams use Sparta and Leonidas AI to move faster, trade smarter, and stay ahead of the market.

At Sparta, you'll be trusted to take ownership, backed by a team who wants you to succeed. AI is how we build here, not just what we sell. Good ideas move fast, and yours could go from staging to production in a couple of hours, whatever department you're in. You'll be challenged, supported, and given room to grow, building the AI that's changing how commodity trading gets done.

Your work has reach. From shaping Leonidas AI, to powering smarter decisions for traders around the world, to changing how commodity trading is done. And because we're growing fast, you'll accelerate your career with a level of ownership and impact you simply won't get at bigger, slower-moving companies.

The role

We’re looking for a London-based Account Manager to own and grow a portfolio of Sparta’s smaller accounts. This is a retention-and-growth role, not a new-logo hunting role: you’ll be the day-to-day commercial owner for a book of existing customers, protecting revenue at renewal and identifying and closing upsell and cross-sell opportunities within it. This is a role for someone a couple of years into account management who wants to progress quickly.

You’ll learn directly from highly experienced Account Directors and take on bigger, more complex accounts as Sparta scales. We’re growing fast, and the room to move up comes with it.

What You’ll Do

• Own a portfolio of smaller accounts, acting as the primary commercial point of contact for each customer.

• Build and execute a renewal plan for every account in your portfolio, working to protect and grow existing ARR.

• Identify and close upsell and cross-sell opportunities (additional seats, products or commodity verticals) within your existing account base.

• Consistently meet retention and expansion targets across your assigned portfolio.

• Run regular check-ins and business reviews with customers to track usage, surface risk early, and reinforce the value Sparta delivers.

• Keep account and opportunity records accurate and up to date in HubSpot, including renewals pipeline and MEDDPICC qualification.

• Partner with Customer Success on onboarding, adoption and usage data to spot expansion and churn-risk signals before they become problems.

• Escalate at-risk accounts promptly and work with the Head of Sales on recovery or win-back plans.

• Support Account Directors on strategic enterprise accounts as needed, building the experience to take on larger accounts and more senior sales responsibility over time

Who You Are

• 3+ years’ experience in an account management role, ideally in B2B SaaS, financial data or commodities.

• Hands-on ownership of both retention and expansion. You’ve run renewals and closed the upsell and cross-sell yourself, rather than passing growth opportunities to a separate salesperson to close.

• Comfortable managing a high volume of smaller accounts at once and prioritising your time effectively.

• A confident relationship-builder with strong written and verbal communication skills.

• Organised and process-driven, with a working knowledge of CRM and AI tools.

• Genuinely curious about commodities and energy markets, with a real appetite to learn.

• Resilient and proactive, comfortable working autonomously in a fast-paced, high-growth environment.

Nice to haves

• Prior exposure to commodities, energy markets, or financial/data services.

• Experience with MEDDPICC or another value-selling framework.

• Familiarity with HubSpot and Claude.

• An additional European language.


Why Join Sparta?

At Sparta, our culture is built on innovation, collaboration, and high performance. We thrive in a fast-paced environment where initiative is celebrated, challenges are embraced, and impact is rewarded.

• Equity in a high-growth, VC-backed company

• $42M in Series B funding — strong market traction and investment

• Early-stage growth — build your career as we scale

• Market-leading product — we are redefining commodity trading intelligence

• Top-tier tools and technology to support your success

What's the Culture Like at Sparta?

At Sparta, our culture isn't just a set of values on a wall — it's how we work. We embrace a dynamic environment where initiative is celebrated, challenges are met head-on, and innovation thrives. You'll collaborate with people who are passionate about our mission and committed to building outstanding products and outcomes for our customers.

The Sparta Code

Understanding is non-negotiable

Understanding leads to believing. Believing leads to winning.

The 'why' is the difference between compliance and conviction. Before we execute, we ask: why does this matter, who does it serve, what changes if we win? People who understand the mission don't need to be managed.

Ask for forgiveness, not for permission

Most decisions are reversible. Most fears are not.

90% of decisions are reversible. Make them, ship, iterate. Perfection is the enemy of efficiency. Bias for action means moving before you have all the answers, but it isn't recklessness. The rule: tell the rest of us what you did, what changed, what you learned.

Fall in love with the problem

The mission wins. Your idea doesn't have to.

Solutions flatter our ego. They feel like progress. But solutions without problems are opinions, and opinions don't move customers, markets, or teammates. The goal is to find what's true, not to win the room. If your idea gets killed because a better one comes along, that's the system working.

It's your fault. Lucky you.

If it's on you, it's in your control.

True ownership sounds harsh until you feel how liberating it is. If every problem is yours, you stop spending energy on who to blame and start spending it on how to fix it. Effective leaders default to 'it's on me'. Not out of guilt, but out of agency.

Conflict is a gift

Honesty is an expression of care.

Withholding feedback is choosing comfort over growth, yours and your colleague's. Staying silent deprives others of the chance to learn. We challenge openly and with positive intent. Done with care, this builds trust. Done with ego, it destroys it.

Sparta Commodities is proud to be an equal opportunity employer and promotes diversity within its workforce. We are determined that no-one will ever receive less favourable treatment on the grounds of gender, age, disability, religion, belief, sexual orientation, marital status, race, veteran status or any basis covered by appropriate law.

  • Own Learning & Development: coaching, training, and levelling up managers and individual contributors

  • Provide executive oversight of workplace and employee experience across all locations. Partner closely with the Executive Team and other leaders to align hiring philosophy, location strategy, and expectations across Sparta's distributed teams

  • Represent People at the leadership table. Raise risks early and make sure stakeholders always know where things stand

What Success Looks Like in Your First Year

  • Executive Team aligned around a clear people strategy

  • Leadership effectiveness and manager capability measurably improved

  • Workforce plan linked to business objectives

  • Salary bands and a levelling framework live

  • Individual scorecards in place, so everyone knows what success looks like for them

  • A structured performance review running company-wide, with buy-in from key stakeholders

  • A middle-management empowerment programme in place, with managers visibly making more decisions without escalating to the exec team

  • Succession plans in place for key roles

  • Hiring on track against plan, with quality and retention holding up

About You

  • You've been the most senior People leader in a scaling organisation, or held a Director or VP People role with significant strategic accountability

  • You've worked in a Series B–D SaaS or tech scaleup and know the people challenges of that stage first-hand

  • You can influence founders, boards and senior executives, and challenge constructively when it's needed

We’re looking for people who thrive in an empowered environment - engineers who are comfortable being given problems to solve rather than solutions to implement. You should enjoy working at pace, value autonomy, and prefer to ask for forgiveness rather than permission. You won’t be handed tickets. You’ll be handed context, and trusted to work out the right thing to build.

  • Keep your services healthy - observability, feedback loops, incident response.

  • Raise the bar around you through code review, pairing and knowledge sharing.

  • 4+ years as a software engineer, with production systems you’ve built and supported.

  • High ownership tendencies

  • Experience in a product-focused organisation, working cross-functionally.

  • Comfortable across multiple languages. We mainly use Kotlin, Java, Python and TypeScript.

  • Able to reason about trade-offs - throughput, latency, consistency, cost - and explain them.

  • At home in system design and in low-level implementation detail.

  • Experience building and deploying services on AWS or GCP.

  • Hands-on exposure to Kafka, Flink, Redis or clustered Postgres, and an appetite for more.

  • Comfortable with agent-based development tools. We use Claude Code; any equivalent is fine.

  • A clear communicator and a pragmatic problem-solver.


NICE TO HAVE EXPERIENCE:

  • Data-intensive applications at scale.

  • Building and interpreting observability - metrics, logging, tracing.

  • Working within or alongside DevOps, SRE or infrastructure teams.

  • Complex distributed environments - high throughput, low latency, large datasets.

jobs.title: Copy of Visiting Brand Designer
jobs.description:
About Peec AI

Peec AI is a Berlin-based Series A startup building analytics and intelligence tools for modern SEO and growth teams. As search rapidly evolves with AI changing how people discover information online, companies need better ways to understand where they appear, how they perform, and where new growth opportunities exist. Peec AI helps teams track their visibility, measure performance, and uncover opportunities to grow their organic presence in an increasingly complex search landscape.

About the role

We're looking for a Visiting Brand Designer to join our team for a minimum 3-months internship and get hands-on with real design.

From week one you'll ship real assets across our website, social, campaigns, and events, and quickly grow into someone the team relies on for sharp, on-brand design.

A big part of the role is being a design partner to people across Peec AI: helping teammates turn ideas into polished, on-brand presentations (internal and external), and tackling the everyday design tasks that keep a fast-moving startup looking sharp. You'll learn how a brand actually gets built and maintained day to day, working side by side with our designers and marketers, and walk away with a portfolio full of real, shipped work.

If you love clean visual craft, exploring different art directions, and iterating your way to something great, and want to learn fast in a high-energy team, this one's for you.

What you'll do

  • Design on-brand assets across marketing channels, social content, campaign visuals, event materials, and web graphics

  • Become our go-to for amazing presentations: transforming internal and external decks into polished, persuasive, on-brand stories

  • Support stakeholders across the company with day-to-day design tasks, helping everyone communicate visually and stay on-brand

  • Work inside our design system and help keep things consistent, scalable, and cohesive

  • Collaborate closely with Growth, Sales, and GEO teams, learning how great brand work comes together end to end

What we're looking for

  • A growing portfolio (university projects, freelance, personal work, all welcome) that shows a strong eye for layout, typography, and visual storytelling

  • Strong working knowledge of Figma, and ideally some Adobe Creative Suite or equivalent

  • Confident presentation design skills, turning information into something clear, structured, and beautiful

  • Detail-obsessed, with the instinct to make things look right, not just done

  • Eager to learn, take feedback, and move quickly in a fast-paced environment

  • Experience in B2B and worked in a startup environment

  • Strong communication skills and a collaborative, can-do attitude

  • Hands-on internship or studio experience, ideally in a B2B or startup environment

Bonus points

  • A strong interest in software products, AI, and emerging tech

  • Experience with motion, animation, or prototyping (After Effects, Lottie, Framer)

What we offer

  • Real ownership and shipped work from week one

  • Close mentorship from experienced brand and growth designers

  • A collaborative, high-energy in-office environment in the heart of Berlin

  • A front-row seat to building a brand in a brand-new market category

  • Paid Dinner & Uber home when working late

  • The most beautiful office space and work environment in Berlin

Compensation: €3K

jobs.title: Mitarbeiter in der Kundenbetreuung (m,f,d)
jobs.description:
Wir suchen eine empathische und kundenorientierte Person, für den Patient:innen Support unserer Kunden. Die Stelle ist zunächst auf ein Jahr befristet. Das Gehalt liegt zwischen 35.000-42.000€ Brutto im Jahr. Die Stelle kann auch Remote durchgeführt werden.

 

Was dich in der Rolle als Mitarbeiter:in in der Kundenbetreuung erwartet

 

Als Mitarbeiter:in in der Kundenbetreuung bist du die Stimme von Nelly für Patient:innen. Mit Empathie, Klarheit und einem guten Gespür für Bedürfnisse begleitest du sie durch aufkommende Fragen. Du sorgst dafür, dass sich die Patient:innen unsere Kund:innen jederzeit gut betreut fühlen.

 

Über Nelly

Wir sind ein Tech-Unternehmen und glauben, dass sich Gesundheitsversorgung deutlich weniger nach Papierkram anfühlen sollte und viel mehr nach Menschen. Deshalb entwickeln wir Technologie, mit der medizinische Praxen einfach, effizient und ohne administratives Chaos arbeiten können.

Unsere Plattform verwandelt komplexe und zeitaufwendige Prozesse in intelligente, automatisierte Workflows – von der Patient Journey über Abrechnung bis hin zu modernen Zahlungslösungen. KI-gestützt, für echte Menschen gebaut und darauf ausgelegt, medizinischen Teams genau das zurückzugeben, was ihnen oft fehlt: Zeit und Fokus. Warum wir das tun? Europa steht vor einem massiven Mangel an medizinischen Fachangestellten. Wenn wir nicht grundlegend neu denken, wie Praxen arbeiten, wird das System langfristig nicht mehr funktionieren. Wir setzen deshalb nicht auf kurzfristige Lösungen, sondern auf echte, nachhaltige Veränderung.

Mit 50 Mio. € Series-B-Finanzierung von führenden internationalen Investor:innen wachsen wir schnell – mit dem Ziel, Europas führendes Healthcare-Fintech aufzubauen. Unsere Vision: Über eine Million medizinische Praxen stärken und das Leben von Millionen Patient:innen spürbar verbessern.

Und das Wichtigste zum Schluss: Wir arbeiten nur mit netten Menschen. Das ist unsere wichtigste Regel. Keine Egos, kein Drama, sondern neugierige, engagierte und empathische Menschen, die gemeinsam etwas Sinnvolles aufbauen wollen.

Wenn sich das nach deinem Ort anfühlt: Willkommen bei Nelly.

Deine Rolle bei uns:

  • Du bist die Stimme von Nelly für Patient:innen, die Nelly nutzen und unterstützt sie mit Empathie, Geduld und einem ausgeprägten Sinn für Details bei allen aufkommendFragen

  • Du kommunizierst auf Augenhöhe und sorgst dafür, dass unsere Kund:innen sich jederzeit gut begleitet fühlen.

  • Du denkst mit und weiter: Kundenfeedback und Verbesserungspotenziale erkennst du frühzeitig und leitest sie gezielt an unser Product Team weiter, um unsere Lösungen stetig besser zu machen.

  • Du arbeitest eng mit Kolleg:innen aus verschiedenen Teams zusammen, insbesondere mit dem Customer Success, Sales und Product Team, denn wir glauben an echte Collaboration über Abteilungen hinweg.

Das bringst du mit:

  • Du bist motiviert und hast Spaß daran mit Kunden in Kontakt zu kommen und diese zu betreuen

  • Du bist zuverlässig und kannst mit deiner strukturierten Arbeitsweise selbstständig arbeiten

  • Du bist kommunikativ stark und trittst selbstsicher in Kundengesprächen auf

  • Du sprichst Deutsch auf muttersprachlichem Niveau

Unsere Benefits:

  • Talent Density. Du arbeitest Seite an Seite mit den klügsten Köpfen, die wir finden konnten: an schwierigen Problemen, als Team. Wir stellen uns Herausforderungen gemeinsam und vergessen dabei nie, Spaß zu haben.

  • Sehr starke Wachstumskurve. Neue Herausforderungen, mehr Verantwortung und echte Ownership vom ersten Tag an. Wir vertrauen darauf, dass du Dinge selbst in die Hand nimmst und dich zu Wort meldest, wenn etwas nicht stimmt. Nur Stillstand solltest du nicht erwarten.

  • Ein jährliches Weiterbildungsbudget, dazu Coaching, Feedback und internes Wissen, das dich wirklich weiterbringt. Wir investieren in deine Entwicklung.

  • Du gestaltest von Anfang an mit, wie wir etwas Großes aufbauen. Wir bauen das finanzielle Betriebssystem für das europäische Gesundheitswesen. KI ist dabei fester Bestandteil davon, wie wir arbeiten.

  • Deutschlandticket oder Swapfiets-Mitgliedschaft.

  • Urban-Sports-Club-Mitgliedschaft.

  • Flexible Arbeitszeiten, ein hybrides Arbeitsmodell und bis zu 4 Wochen Workation.

  • Ein hundefreundliches Büro.

Wir leben Vielfalt und freuen uns über Bewerbungen von Menschen aller Geschlechter (m/w/d). Und weil wir wissen, dass Selbstzweifel oder das sogenannte Impostor-Syndrom oft davon abhalten, sich zu bewerben, gilt: Zögere nicht, auch wenn du nicht jedes einzelne Kriterium erfüllst. Wenn du überzeugt bist, dass du gut zu uns passt, sag uns warum – wir freuen uns ehrlich darauf, von dir zu hören.

jobs.title: Global Investigator (Triage)
jobs.description:
Build a Safer World.

TRM Labs provides AI-powered intelligence solutions that help public and private sector agencies investigate and disrupt crime. TRM's platforms enable investigators to trace illicit activity, build cases, and construct operating pictures of threat networks. Leading agencies and businesses worldwide rely on TRM to make the world safer and more secure.

As a Global Investigator on the triage team, you will be the first line of operational defense in a fast-moving crypto disruption pipeline. You will process inbound complaint data, validate outputs from our artificial-intelligence (AI) investigation platform, and route cases into the investigative pipelines that result in frozen scam proceeds and seized assets. You will hold the disposition pen: your call is what turns a complaint into a freeze, a takedown, a recovery handoff, a legal-process draft, a victim notification, or a close.

The impact you will have:

  • Validate and route hundreds of complaint dispositions per week, feeding a live asset-recovery pipeline.

  • Catch the AI errors that matter, such as false positives, merged syndicates, and misclassified scam patterns, before they propagate downstream.

  • Enrich complaint selectors using a stack of more than forty commercial data-source integrations.

  • Own clean shift handoffs so the around-the-clock operation never drops a lead, providing EMEA-hours coverage that keeps the queue moving while colleagues in other regions are offline.

What we’re looking for:

  • Investigative or analytical experience in the private or public sector. One to three years is fine: we want hungry people who want to grow into deep crypto expertise.

  • Strong AI fluency, meaning comfort using AI tools as a daily co-pilot, plus the judgment to know when they are wrong.

  • Excitement to deepen blockchain analysis skills.

  • Comfort operating in a fast-paced, fluid environment where the project's scope and emphasis may shift quarter to quarter.

  • Strong written and verbal communication.

About the Team:

  • The team is built around a mix of seasoned investigators and rising talent. Triage investigators sit alongside experienced crypto tracers and intelligence-trained individual contributors, and the seat is designed to accelerate your development.

Team Operating Rhythms:

  • Daily schedule: standard business hours in your local time zone.

  • Collaboration: coordinate with global teammates for handoffs on time-sensitive items, giving the wider operation near follow-the-sun coverage.

On-Call Responsibilities:

  • Formal on-call rotation for high-priority events, such as hacks, law-enforcement support, and other time-sensitive matters.

  • Weekly rotation, with occasional weekend coverage as needed.

Learn about TRM Speed in this position:

  • React quickly to incoming complaint surges and live takedown events.

  • Continuously learn new patterns in crypto-enabled crime.

Application Instructions

If you’re interested in joining TRM, we encourage you to apply directly. Every application is reviewed by our Talent team.

Before applying, review the job description carefully and highlight the experience and impact that best demonstrate the required qualifications. Please also provide thoughtful and accurate answers to the application questions, as these will be used to evaluate your skills and qualifications for the role.

If you send your resume directly to someone at TRM, we can’t guarantee it will reach the appropriate hiring team. Applying directly is the best way to ensure your application will be considered.

Interviewing with TRM

Our process is designed to understand how you think, solve problems, and deliver impact, while allowing you to evaluate TRM. Most interview processes include a case study, an AI skills assessment, and a Leadership Principles interview.

  • Recruiter Intro: Qualifications, motivations, and alignment with the role.

  • Hiring Manager: Deep dive into your relevant experience, skills, and impact.

  • First Round: 1–2 interviews focused on the skills most critical to the role.

  • Final Round: Hands-on case study. This is usually a panel-style session where we go deeper into your craft, problem-solving, and alignment with TRM.

  • References: Former colleagues who can provide insight into your work and impact.

  • Offer: Congrats! Your recruiter will present the offer and compensation details.

  • Welcome to TRM: We're excited to build a safer world with you!

Your recruiter will share your specific interview plan and preparation guidance along the way.

AI Fluency at TRM

AI fluency is a baseline expectation at TRM.

We believe AI meaningfully changes how top performers operate. We expect every team member to use AI to accelerate and reimagine their craft, not just automate surface tasks.

At TRM, AI fluency means you are among the top 10 percent of operators in your function in how you apply AI to:

  • Accelerate repeatable workflows

  • Structure and solve problems

  • Improve output quality

  • Increase speed and leverage

You will be evaluated on applied AI fluency during the interview process.

Life at TRM

We are building a safer world. That promise shows up in how we work every day.

TRM moves FAST. We are a high-velocity, high-ownership team that expects clarity, follow-through, and impact. People who thrive here are energized by hard problems, experimentation, and continuous feedback. If something takes months elsewhere, it will ship here in days.

Our work sits at the intersection of AI, national security, and fighting crime. The problems are complex, the stakes are real, and the environment evolves quickly. The pace and intensity of the work reflect the importance of the mission. As a result, the way we operate requires a high level of ownership, adaptability, collaboration, and creative problem-solving.

At TRM, you should expect:

  • Priorities and targets to change quickly

  • Operating with a high degree of ambiguity

  • A high level of personal ownership and accountability

  • Close collaboration across teams and functions

  • Frequent, high-touch communication

  • Creative problem-solving and out-of-the-box thinking

  • A pace that rewards urgency, adaptability, and outcomes

This environment is energizing for people who enjoy building, solving hard problems, and making progress in situations that are not always fully defined. It also requires thriving in ambiguity, adjusting course as new information emerges, and maintaining focus and positivity in a fast-moving and intense environment.

We also recognize that this style of operating is not for everyone. If you are primarily optimizing for predictability or a consistently balanced workload, we encourage you to use the interview process to pressure-test whether this environment is truly the right fit. We want teammates who thrive here, not just survive here.

If you are excited by meaningful problems, motivated by ambitious goals, and energized by working alongside mission-driven colleagues, there is a good chance you will find TRM to be an exceptional place to grow and contribute.

Leadership Principles

We hire and grow against three leadership principles. They’re the standards for how we operate, treat each other, and make decisions.

  • Impact-Oriented Trailblazer: We put customers first and move with speed, focus, and adaptability. We treat every plan like an experiment – test, ship, measure, and iterate quickly.

  • Master Craftsperson: We care deeply about our craft. We balance speed with high standards, own outcomes end‑to‑end, and invest in getting better everyday.

  • Inspiring Colleague: We add clarity and energy, not noise. We bring humility, candor, and a one‑team mindset — giving and receiving feedback to make the team stronger.

Join our Mission

At TRM, we care deeply about our craft. We are looking for individuals who want their work to matter, who experiment with speed and rigor, and who take pride in building a safer world for billions of people. If you’re excited by TRM’s mission but don’t check every box, we encourage you to apply — we hire for slope, judgment, and the will to learn fast.

TRM is a Series C company with $220M in total funding, backed by Goldman Sachs, Bessemer, Y Combinator, Thoma Bravo, and others. Headquartered in San Francisco, TRM operates as a distributed-first company with hubs in Los Angeles, San Francisco, New York, Washington D.C., London, and Singapore.

jobs.description:
About Us:

DeepJudge is Switzerland’s leading AI and ICT scale-up, transforming how law firms and legal departments access and leverage their knowledge. Founded by former Google search engineers with PhDs in AI from ETH Zurich, and backed by top-tier Silicon Valley investors, we are building the intelligence layer that powers the legal industry.

Every firm can license the same AI models, but no two firms share the same institutional knowledge. Decades of experience, work product, and precedent are often trapped across systems, underused and inaccessible. DeepJudge makes this expertise instantly available through world-class enterprise search and AI infrastructure, enabling firms to automate workflows, build knowledge-powered applications, and turn experience into a lasting advantage.

Our technology is trusted by many of the world’s leading law firms, including Freshfields, Gunderson Dettmer, Holland & Knight, Arent Fox, and Cozen O’Connor. Headquartered in Switzerland with a growing team across North America, we are expanding rapidly and shaping the future of how professional knowledge is discovered and applied.

At DeepJudge, we move fast, think rigorously, and care deeply about what we build. We combine cutting-edge research with close collaboration with our clients to deliver solutions that truly make an impact. If you want to be part of a team defining how AI transforms high-stakes knowledge work, this is the place to do it.


About the role:

As a Site Reliability Engineer at DeepJudge, you own the reliability of the systems that leading law firms depend on every day. We run our AI search platform in dedicated production environments, each a large-scale search and retrieval system operating at very high data volumes, alongside our ingestion pipelines and data stores, on container-orchestrated infrastructure across multiple public and private clouds. Keeping those environments fast, available, and trustworthy is a genuine engineering challenge, and it's your mission.

This is a technical, infrastructure-focused role: you'll spend your time in systems, code, and telemetry. You'll harden the platform so that classes of failure can't recur, build observability and SLOs to let us see problems before they surface, plan capacity ahead of relentless data growth, and automate away the toil of safely operating many production environments. You'll work across our deployment and infrastructure-as-code and partner closely with product engineering to feed reliability learnings back into the platform. If you like operating serious distributed systems at scale and turning firefighting into engineered reliability, this role is for you.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Owning the availability, latency and performance of our production environments: large-scale search and retrieval services, ingestion and data stores on container-orchestrated infrastructure across multiple public and private clouds

  • Owning the cloud infrastructure across multiple public and private clouds, networking, identity and access, compute and storage, and managing cloud capacity, quotas and cost as the fleet grows

  • Improving deployment and infrastructure through code: GitOps-based configuration and deployment and infrastructure-as-code across our public and private clouds, with safe, previewed, recoverable production changes

  • Defining and instrumenting SLOs and error budgets and building the dashboards, metrics and alerting that make production observable and actionable

  • Reducing operational toil through automation and internal tooling written in Python and / or Go

  • Provisioning and standardizing new production environments to a defined reliability bar

You're a great fit if you:

  • Have 3+ years in SRE, production / platform engineering, or infrastructure-heavy software engineering, operating real production systems under reliability expectations

  • Are strong at container-orchestration operations in production and comfortable on at least one major public cloud

  • Have solid cloud infrastructure experience on a major public cloud and a working grasp of cloud capacity, quotas, and cost

  • Practice observability hands-on with metrics, logs and traces, and use it to root-cause live incidents

  • Work fluently with infrastructure-as-code and GitOps

  • Can code in Python and / or Go for automation, tooling, and reading and patching service code.

  • Bring sound production judgment and document your work clearly for other engineers

  • Bonus: experience operating a large-scale search or distributed data system, database operations, dedicated / enterprise-deployed software, or AI / enterprise-search infrastructure in regulated domains

What you can look forward to:

  • Owning the reliability of systems that the world's leading law firms rely on: real scale, real impact

  • Deep, hands-on work with modern infrastructure: distributed search at very large scale, container orchestration across multiple clouds, and a mature infrastructure-as-code and GitOps stack

  • A rigorous, high-urgency engineering culture founded by ex-Google search engineers and ETH Zurich AI PhDs

  • The chance to build the reliability discipline, SLOs, incident practice, automation, from a strong foundation, not inherit a rigid one

  • A collaborative team in Zurich shaping how AI transforms professional knowledge work

At DeepJudge, we believe great teams are built on diverse perspectives and experiences. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer and are committed to fostering an inclusive, high-performance culture where everyone can thrive. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and do not discriminate based on race, religion, color, national origin, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

jobs.title: Director of Engineering
jobs.description:
Who we are

Foundation models transformed text and images. Structured data - the largest and most consequential data format in the world - stayed untouched, until now. What LLMs did for language, we're doing for tables.

We pioneered tabular foundation models: TabPFN v2 was a Nature cover story, has passed 3.5M+ downloads and 7,500+ GitHub stars, and runs in production from detecting lung disease with Oxford Cancer Analytics to preventing train failures with Hitachi. The hardest problems - millions of rows, real-time inference, entirely new modalities - are still open, and no one else is working on them at this level.

We're a small, highly selective team of 40+ with backgrounds from Google, DeepMind, Meta, Apple, Amazon, Jane Street, and CERN, led by Frank Hutter, Noah Hollmann, and Sauraj Gambhir, and advised by Bernhard Schölkopf and Turing Award winner Yann LeCun.

In July 2026, less than 18 months after our €9M pre-seed, we joined SAP as an independent frontier AI lab - same team, mission, and open-weights models, now backed by more than €1 billion over four years.

The role

You will be our first dedicated engineering leader, reporting to the CTO with a direct line to both founders - no layers in between.

Today, engineering at Prior Labs is a small, very senior team. We plan to grow it substantially over the next 18 months, and your job is to build and run that organization.

We want to be honest about what this job is. It is a hands-on operator role: managing engineers, building the hiring machine, setting standards, running compliance, and working closely with our partners at SAP. If you light up at making an organization fast rather than at owning the biggest possible headcount, this is your role.

What you'll do

  • Directly manage and grow the engineering team, including building out its management layer.

  • Build the hiring machine: run hiring operations across our hiring managers, design interview loops that hold up in the AI era, and keep a very high bar while the team grows.

  • Own engineering standards and velocity: how we review, test, and ship - and how the team gets real leverage from AI coding tools.

  • Own our security and compliance program - SOC 2, GDPR, ISO 27001 - right-sized, so the lab keeps its speed.

  • Own the engineering side of our collaboration with SAP.

  • Treat the deployment layer as a product surface: our models reach customers through a managed API, customer VPCs, and self-hosted open weights, and the engineering behind that needs customer empathy, not just platform craft.

  • Act as a sparring partner to the founders on org design and engineering direction - we're hiring someone who will argue with us.

What we're looking for

  • You have directly led an engineering organization of 10+ people, including through managers or leads, and you can talk concretely about how you built it.

  • You have owned platform or infrastructure scope at scale: serving, APIs, availability, cloud and vendor budgets.
