jobs.title: Knit - Research Manager
jobs.description:
Knit is the AI-native consumer research platform helping brands automate and accelerate primary research. With our Researcher-Driven AI, we’ve condensed the entire quant + qual research process from weeks into days (sometimes hours!) for 50+ enterprise brands — including Amazon, T-Mobile, Mars, NASCAR, and more. We’re on a mission to scale and democratize world-class research. From survey generation to stakeholder-ready reports, our platform is redefining how insights teams operate — and we need your help to push the limits of what’s possible.


Overview

The purpose of the Research Manager role is to ensure Knit customers successfully achieve their desired research outcomes through their partnerships with Knit. By owning and supporting customer relationships, getting deeply engrained in customer research needs, and driving high-quality project deliverables, the Research Manager’s impact is ultimately measured by positive customer retention.

Responsibilities:

The research function is a primary contributor to Knit’s shared business objectives of customer retention and upsells, ultimately measured by Net Revenue Retention (NRR) in addition to supporting successful Pilot to Subscription Conversions for acquiring new business.

The levers the Research Manager role owns to influence these key business objectives are:

  • Research Success → Ensuring Knit Customers successfully achieve their desired research outcomes through their projects with Knit, measured by successfully achieving Research Objectives and delivering on Knit’s Quality & Speed service-level agreements (SLA’s)

Primary responsibilities of this role:

  • Serving as the dedicated research lead for all customers’ projects (on assigned accounts) and serving as the ultimate accountable part for research project success

  • Driving and documenting in-depth project scoping to uncover a deep understanding of research objectives and project context to set up project success

  • Demonstrate a growth mindset as a solutions architect for customers, educating them on Knit’s research capabilities, consulting with them to adjust for fringe requirements, and proposing solutions to maximize project success - escalating to Research Directors when needs exceed capabilities

  • Escalating needs to Research Directors to support troubleshooting when increased risk for project viability or customer impact occurs

  • Driving, maintaining, and enriching all customer context to improve Knit’s ability to meet the customers’ custom research needs

  • Being the final, customer-ready check and approver on all Knit final topline delivery and presenting the key insights and recommendations directly to the customers

  • Participating in continuous innovation on Knit’s AI product to minimize the delta between Knit’s AI output and a human researcher output

  • Driving on feedback collection on “the last mile” - uncovering and documenting what happens after Knit delivers a project to when it’s “stakeholder ready,” supporting Knit’s product vision in getting to stakeholder ready reports

Required Skills & Experiences:

  • Must have 5+ years of market research experience, with the majority of the time spent on the supplier side in a market research agency environment.

  • Must have experience leading discovery and scoping calls, writing and editing quant and qual questionnaires from scratch, drafting analysis plans, and creating and presenting stakeholder-ready insights topline & reports.

  • Ability to drive initiatives and outcomes in ambiguous environments, both for navigating complex customer needs and Knit internal business changes. Proven track record successfully operating in an early stage startup (<50 employees) is a plus.

  • Proven track record of owning and supporting client relationships with customers at Enterprise, Fortune 500 US-based companies, specifically working with insights professionals to scope and achieve desired research outcomes, resulting in customer retention and growth.

  • Ability to drive initiatives and outcomes successfully in environments with competing priorities, multiple research projects on at a given time, and simultaneous internal business demands.

Benefits

Upon joining the Knit team, you will receive a competitive salary + commission plan if applicable to role, Equity Options, Healthcare (medical, dental, and vision), and Additional Coverage, a company laptop and one-time, onboarding Technology Stipend, a 401(k) with company match, flexible time-off, hybrid working, and more!

Salary

In accordance with New York pay transparency requirements, the salary range for this role is $115,000 - $130,000. Final compensation will be determined based on the candidate’s level, experience, and qualifications upon joining Knit.

Our Company Values

We are the Championship Team. This means we:

  • Are 1% better every day: We approach situations with a growth mindset and ask, “How can we make the business better?” and “What would it take?”

  • Play to win: We set audacious goals and push ourselves to achieve them with a bias towards action (When we see a need, we take initiative, and hold ourselves accountable to seeing it through).

  • Keep the main thing the main thing: Identify what has the biggest impact and prioritize to focus on it.

jobs.title: System Architect
jobs.description:
Are you an experienced System Architect with a passion for intelligent building management systems, industrial automation, and safety-critical applications? At Deerns, you will have the opportunity to work on innovative and challenging projects that contribute to a smarter, safer, and more sustainable future. Read on and discover how you can make an impact.

The challenge 

The System Architect for Intelligent Building Management Solutions and Industrial Automation plays a crucial role in designing integrated automation solutions for both buildings and industrial processes. This position involves developing safe, efficient, and future-ready systems that connect various installations, such as HVAC, lighting, access control, gas safety, and industrial process control. You will work closely with project teams, suppliers, and end-users to create innovative and sustainable solutions that meet the highest safety standards.

Your responsibilities include: 

  • Developing automation architectures: Design scalable solutions for intelligent building management and process automation, including gas detection systems, safety mechanisms, and process control.

  • System integration: Connect installations using protocols like BACnet, Modbus, KNX, and industrial standards such as OPC UA and PROFIBUS.

  • Gas safety and process safety: Develop solutions for gas detection, emergency shutdowns, ventilation integration, and fail-safe control systems for industrial environments.

  • Specification and standards management: Implement relevant standards for intelligent building management solutions, process automation, and safety systems, such as IEC 61511 (functional safety) and ATEX regulations.

  • Process optimization: Analyze and optimize industrial processes and systems to enhance efficiency, safety, and sustainability.

  • Stakeholder management: Collaborate effectively with various stakeholders, including clients, end-users, engineers, and project managers, ensuring solutions meet both functional and technical requirements.

  • Continuous learning and development: Stay updated on the latest innovations in smart technologies and automation, applying these to develop improved, future-proof solutions. • Technological consulting: Identify innovations to enhance performance and reliability in intelligent buildings and industrial environments.

  • Documentation and communication: Prepare technical documentation and communicate effectively with multidisciplinary teams and stakeholders.

Required Skills and Competencies:

  • Extensive knowledge of intelligent building management solutions, gas safety systems, and industrial process control.

  • Expertise in communication standards and protocols such as KNX, BACnet, Modbus, OPC UA, and PROFIBUS.

  • Proficiency in designing fail-safe systems and safety-critical applications.

  • Experience with IT networks and cybersecurity in automation environments.

  • Strong analytical skills and problem-solving abilities.

  • Flexibility and the ability to continuously adapt to technological advancements.

  • Excellent communication skills to clearly present complex technical issues

Education and Experience:

  • Bachelor’s or master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Automation Technology, or a related field.

  • Relevant experience in intelligent building management solutions, industrial automation, and safety-critical systems. This role combines technological innovation with safety-critical applications. As a System Architect, you will develop integrated solutions that maximize comfort, safety, efficiency, and sustainability in both buildings and industrial processes.

We offer 

  • A position of 32-40 hours per week with a salary to match. 

  • Challenging projects for leading clients in the Netherlands and internationally. 

  • A work environment in which innovation and sustainability are put into practice daily. 

  • Attention to your own development and vitality with ample training and development opportunities, bicycle and sports arrangements, flexible working hours, 33 vacation days and the possibility of purchasing additional days.

jobs.title: Director Operations & Safety (m/w/d)

Als Leiter Betrieb und Sicherheit (m/w/d) verantwortest du das operative Herz von FlixTrain: von der Betriebs- und Produktionsplanung über die Leitstelle, die in Echtzeit den Betrieb steuert, bis hin zur Betriebssicherheit, der Flottendisposition sowie dem Partner- und Qualitätsmanagement. Du sorgst für einen sicheren, pünktlichen, zuverlässigen und kundenfreundlichen Zugbetrieb und baust das Führungsteam über alle operativen Funktionen hinweg auf – mit direkter Berichtslinie an den CEO.
Wir suchen eine Persönlichkeit, die unternehmerisch handelt und entscheidet, für die Sache brennt, mit anpackt und Lust am Aufbau von Strukturen, Prozessen und Optimierungen hat. Bei uns kannst du den Betrieb des größten privaten Fernverkehrsplayers in Deutschland aufbauen.

Über die Rolle

  • Du verantwortest Betriebsplanung, Produktionskonzepte sowie Schicht- und Personaleinsatzplanung für einen zuverlässigen und sicheren Betrieb.

  • Du verantwortest gemeinsam mit dem Safety Manager die Eisenbahnsicherheit, die regulatorische Compliance und die Sicherheitskultur – inklusive der Safety-Teams und Betriebskontrolleure.

  • Du definierst mit deinem Team die Anforderungen an unsere Software-Entwicklung, Automatisierung und Digitalisierung von Abläufen, harmonisierst die Software-Landschaft und sorgst für eine gute Anwendbarkeit über alle Funktionen hinweg.

Über Dich

  • Du bringst ein unternehmerisches Mindset und echte Leidenschaft fürs Aufbauen mit – du brennst für das Ergebnis und packst mit an, um es Wirklichkeit werden zu lassen.

Bei uns zählt der Blick auf das Ganze – auch wenn du nicht alle Anforderungen zu 100 % erfüllst, aber dennoch glaubst, etwas bewegen zu können, freuen wir uns auf deine Bewerbung! 

Was Wir Bieten

  • Gestaltungsspielraum mit Mandat: Eine Schlüsselrolle mit direkter Berichtslinie an den CEO und dem Auftrag, den Betrieb des größten privaten Fernverkehrsanbieters Deutschlands maßgeblich aufzubauen – dein Einfluss ist unmittelbar sichtbar.

Warum Teil von Flix werden? 

Bei Flix konzentrieren wir uns darauf, Reisen einfach, sicher und erschwinglich zu gestalten – sowohl für unsere Passagiere als auch für unsere Mitarbeiter. Wenn du einen Job suchst, in dem du wachsen und etwas bewirken kannst, dann bist du bei FlixTrain genau richtig. Hier kannst du Teil eines Teams werden, in dem dein Beitrag zählt und du deine Reise selbst gestalten kannst!

jobs.title: Senior Backend Engineer (Golang) - Bank Balance
jobs.description:
At SumUp, the Global Bank team builds the core infrastructure and services that give merchants a digital bank account, helping small businesses manage their money easily and reliably. 

The Balance Management Squad sits at the core of the Global Bank Platform. Right now, our team is completing a major milestone: consolidating and modernizing our balance management system in Europe. The next big step is creating a global transaction history service; a single, shared platform used by all regions to give merchants consistent and transparent views of their financial activity.

As a Senior Backend Engineer, you'll help modernize existing systems while balancing innovation with stability, collaborate with teams across regions, and build reliable services that manage diverse markets with different regulations.

If you enjoy solving complex problems on high-load systems, are curious about banking, and are looking for a team that tackles challenges head-on, we'd love to hear from you.

What You'll Do

  • Build and evolve the SumUp's core banking services that powers ledger operations and transactions, transforming our regional systems into a unified, scalable global platform.
  • Tackle complex distributed systems challenges, ensuring resilient services that continue to perform under high transaction volumes.
  • Support modernization initiatives by improving observability, adding test coverage, refactoring code for long-term maintainability, and gradually introducing new architectural patterns without disrupting live banking operations.
  • Contribute to key architectural decisions - build ledger and transaction history systems from the ground up, ensuring a globally scalable banking solution for our clients.
  • Collaborate with teams across Risk, Treasury, Finance, and Infrastructure to ensure smooth, compliant, and reliable global operations
  • Take ownership from design to production, running the services you build, monitoring their performance, and continuously improving how we deliver high-quality software at scale.

You'll be great for this role if

  • You have solid backend experience building reliable, high-volume services and you think carefully about system design, APIs, data modeling, and how services interact.
  • You are proficient in Golang and comfortable learning and working with other languages as needed, e.g. Kotlin or Elixir.
  • You write maintainable, well-tested code, follow CI/CD best practices, and take responsibility for the software you build from development to production.
  • You're comfortable building, deploying, and running services in cloud environments like AWS using Docker and Kubernetes.
  • Are fluent in relational databases that perform well under load and maintain data consistency.
  • You are a collaborator who enjoys working across regions, communicating clearly, exchanging feedback effectively, and making thoughtful technical decisions together.
  • You have a curiosity for building reliable financial services and banking domain

It's a plus if you have

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer, Operations Foundations
jobs.description:
About Wolt

At Wolt, we create technology that brings joy, simplicity and earnings to the neighborhoods of the world. In 2014 we started with delivery of restaurant food. Now we're building the delivery of (almost) everything and you'll find us in over 500 cities in 30 countries around the world. In 2022 we joined forces with DoorDash and together we keep on dreaming big and expanding across the globe.

Working at Wolt isn't always easy, but it's definitely exciting. Here you'll learn more, build more, and ship more than in most other companies. You'll be challenged a lot, but also have a lot of fun on the way. So, if you're a self-starter with drive and entrepreneurial spirit, this could be the ride of your life.

Wolt is looking for a Senior Software Engineer (Front-end-leaning) to join our Operations Foundations team. The team sits within the DoorDash Client and AI Development group and is responsible for the foundation that hundreds of engineers across Wolt, DoorDash, and Deliveroo rely on to build internal operations tools. Our platform hosts 250+ micro-frontends (MFEs) used to operate every part of the business.

Our team is focused on building a scalable, reliable, and high-quality internal tooling platform that supports Wolt, DoorDash, and Deliveroo's operations and business.

The team plays an important role in improving how engineers build, test, and ship software across the organization, with a strong emphasis on reusable libraries, micro-frontend architecture, and agentic development: building the platform where AI agents can take changes from task to merged PR safely and reliably without lowering the quality bar.

Currently, we are focused on unifying our frontend platforms, evolving shared components and library development, improving developer productivity, and enabling teams to deliver more independently through better architecture and tooling.

It's an exciting time to join because the team has strong ownership and a broad technical impact.

We're looking for a Senior Software Engineer who can take ownership of complex technical initiatives across both frontend and sometimes backend and infra domains. In this role, you'll work primarily with TypeScript, React, Node.js, CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions, Buildkite), and MFE architecture to build scalable, maintainable solutions that support multiple product teams and business areas.

Success in this role means becoming a trusted technical owner who consistently delivers reliable solutions and helps the team execute more effectively. Six months into the role, we'd expect you to be independently leading technical initiatives and contributing meaningfully to architecture and delivery planning.

This role offers the opportunity to solve challenging engineering problems with visible impact across the business. It's especially exciting for someone who enjoys combining product engineering with platform thinking, improving developer workflows, and building systems that scale across teams and domains.

What you'll be doing

  • Owning the Foundation: the runtime, build, deployment, and developer experience that 250+ MFEs and hundreds of engineers depend on every day.
  • Evolving Our Micro-Frontend Architecture: improve composition, isolation, and shared dependency strategies so feature teams can move fast.
  • Product and Planning: Independently drive projects from idea to production: breaking down ambiguous problems into clear technical plans, estimating delivery, identifying risks early, and delivering high-quality solutions in a timely manner.
  • Supporting Engineering Excellence: Champion best practices, raise the bar for code quality, and turn lessons learned into platform improvements.
  • Long-Term Thinking: Balance short-term feature unblockers with the long-term health, security, and maintainability of the platform.
  • Agentic Development: Build the foundations that let AI agents work autonomously on our platform, including agent instructions, reusable skills, tool integrations, guardrails, and the automated checks that make agent-authored changes safe to ship.
  • AI Fluency: Work agent-first in your own day-to-day: delegate implementation to agents, and focus your judgment on direction, architecture, and verifying outcomes.

📍This role can be based in our Berlin tech hub. Read more about our hybrid setup here.

Feel free to check out the Wolt Tech Blog for more insight into our culture and technology.

Our humble expectations

  • Proven expertise in building production frontend applications using TypeScript and React.
  • Solid backend knowledge, comfortable owning and operating Node.js services that support frontend infrastructure.
  • Strong knowledge of frontend build tools, bundlers, and module systems, and the ability to evolve them as the platform grows.
  • Track record of diagnosing and resolving complex performance, reliability, or DX issues in large frontend codebases.
  • Experience driving technical initiatives across multiple engineering teams and stakeholders.
  • Strong stakeholder management skills: aligning priorities, managing expectations, and communicating trade-offs clearly with partner teams and leadership.
  • Strong communication skills and a collaborative, platform-mindset approach to working with feature teams.
  • Strong documentation skills, including experience writing RFCs or ADRs.

Nice to Haves

  • Experience with micro-frontend architecture.
  • Frontend platform engineering experience.
  • Experience building shared component libraries used by many product teams.
  • Hands-on experience with CI/CD pipelines, deployment processes, and cloud infrastructure for frontend workloads.
  • Experience or interest in observability and reliability (SRE).
  • Experience building tooling or workflows for autonomous AI coding agents (e.g., agent instructions, skills, MCP servers, or evaluating agent-generated code).

What's in it for you

  • Impact: Build and shape the platform that thousands of people depend on.
  • Scale: Work on real platform problems behind 250+ MFEs with hundreds of monthly contributors.
  • Collaboration: Partner with talented engineers, designers, and operators across companies to make their daily work faster and better.
  • Growth: Take on deep technical challenges across frontend architecture, agentic development, DX, and improving engineering efficiency.
  • Culture: Be part of a diverse, open-minded team that values creativity, autonomy, and continuous learning.

Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion

We're committed to growing and empowering a more inclusive community within our company, industry, and cities. That's why we hire and cultivate diverse teams of people from all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We believe that true innovation happens when everyone has room at the table and the tools, resources, and opportunity to excel.

Beware of recruitment scams: DoorDash, Deliveroo, and Wolt will never ask you to pay money or share sensitive financial information during hiring — learn more about our legitimate recruiting process at Recruitment Scam Awareness - DoorDash .

🚀 Apporteur d’affaires indépendant — Développez votre réseau avec PropertyOS

100 % à distance · Organisation libre · Commission sur les ventes issues de vos recommandations

Vous aimez créer des contacts, repérer des opportunités et mettre les bonnes personnes en relation ?

Avec PropertyOS, vous identifiez des propriétaires, bailleurs ou petites agences intéressés par une gestion immobilière plus simple. Vous organisez le rendez-vous : le fondateur assure la démonstration et le closing.

🏡 PropertyOS, c’est quoi ?

PropertyOS est une plateforme SaaS qui centralise les biens immobiliers, les locataires, les finances, les documents et les tâches dans un même espace.

Notre ambition : permettre aux propriétaires et gestionnaires de gagner du temps et de garder une vision claire de leur activité immobilière.

La plateforme est accessible directement en ligne. Nous développons également un réseau de partenaires indépendants pour la faire découvrir à de nouveaux clients grâce à une approche plus personnelle.

🎯 Votre mission : créer des opportunités qualifiées

Votre rôle consiste à :

  • Identifier des propriétaires bailleurs, investisseurs et petites agences susceptibles d’être intéressés.

  • Entrer en contact avec eux et comprendre leur organisation actuelle.

  • Présenter simplement PropertyOS et son intérêt.

  • Vérifier leur intérêt pour une démonstration et pour le budget proposé.

  • Organiser un rendez-vous avec le fondateur.

  • Enregistrer les informations utiles dans PropertyOS Advisor pour préparer l’échange.

Vous vous concentrez sur la prospection et la mise en relation. Le fondateur prend ensuite le relais pour la démonstration détaillée, les questions commerciales, la négociation et la conclusion de l’abonnement.

Vous ne négociez pas les conditions et ne signez pas de contrat au nom de PropertyOS.

⚡ PropertyOS Advisor : votre application partenaire

Vous disposez de PropertyOS Advisor, notre application dédiée aux apporteurs d’affaires.

Pensée pour fluidifier votre activité, elle vous permet de centraliser les informations de vos prospects, suivre vos mises en relation et transmettre le contexte nécessaire à la préparation des rendez-vous.

L’objectif : une prospection organisée et un passage de relais simple, pour donner à chaque opportunité les meilleures chances d’aboutir.

💸 Une rémunération liée aux clients apportés

L’offre mise en avant dans ce partenariat est l’abonnement annuel PropertyOS à 990 €.

Vous percevez une commission pour chaque nouveau client qui souscrit et règle cet abonnement à la suite de votre mise en relation, selon les conditions prévues au contrat.

  • Rémunération à la commission uniquement.

  • Aucun salaire fixe ni revenu garanti.

  • Le montant de la commission et le calendrier de versement sont communiqués avant tout engagement.

  • Les règles d’attribution des prospects, de traitement des doublons et d’annulation sont précisées au contrat.

  • Un rendez-vous seul ne déclenche pas de commission : celle-ci dépend de la souscription et de l’encaissement correspondants.

👋 À qui s’adresse cette opportunité ?

À des personnes autonomes, à l’aise dans les échanges et capables de créer un premier contact de qualité.

Vous pouvez avoir une expérience commerciale, un réseau dans l’immobilier ou simplement une vraie capacité à prospecter avec méthode.

Nous recherchons surtout :

  • De l’écoute, pour repérer un besoin réel.

  • De la clarté, pour expliquer la solution sans faire de promesses excessives.

  • De la régularité, pour développer votre activité.

  • De la rigueur, pour transmettre des informations fiables.

  • Un bon relationnel, pour représenter PropertyOS avec professionnalisme.

Une expérience en prospection, en immobilier ou dans le SaaS est un atout. Vous n’avez pas besoin d’être un expert du logiciel ni un closer confirmé.

🌴 Notre culture : détendue, directe et orientée résultats

Chez PropertyOS, on apprécie les échanges simples, les idées utiles et les personnes qui prennent des initiatives.

Vous organisez librement votre activité : pas d’horaires imposés ni de volume hebdomadaire obligatoire. Cette collaboration peut compléter d’autres activités professionnelles.

Notre façon d’avancer : partager les retours du terrain, améliorer les approches et privilégier des mises en relation pertinentes.

Une ambiance chill, des engagements tenus et des opportunités concrètes.

🤝 Pour bien démarrer

La prise en main comprend :

  • Une présentation de PropertyOS et de ses principaux cas d’usage.

  • La découverte de PropertyOS Advisor.

  • Des repères pour identifier les profils de clients recherchés.

  • Des supports pour présenter la solution.

  • Une explication du processus de mise en relation et de rémunération.

Vous avez un interlocuteur direct pour transmettre vos questions et vos retours.

📋 Cadre de la collaboration

Nature : partenariat indépendant d’apport d’affaires, sans contrat de travail.
Lieu : à distance, depuis la France.
Organisation : libre, sans exclusivité.
Démarrage : à convenir ensemble.

Vous devez disposer d’une activité indépendante déclarée et d’un SIRET pour exercer depuis la France. La micro-entreprise est une possibilité.

Vous pouvez candidater avant d’avoir créé votre activité, mais les formalités nécessaires devront être réalisées pour démarrer la collaboration.

Un contrat écrit définit les missions, les commissions et les conditions du partenariat.

🚀 Intéressé ? Présentez-vous simplement.

Envoyez-nous quelques lignes sur :

  • Votre parcours et votre éventuelle expérience en prospection.

  • Les types de prospects que vous pourriez contacter.

  • Votre statut actuel et vos disponibilités pour démarrer.

Vous créez le contact. Nous prenons le relais pour transformer l’intérêt en abonnement.

jobs.description:
ennovationHUB is an expanding international e-commerce group specialising in the home & living sector, with furniture at the core of our offering. Through our hubs in Belgrade, Barcelona, and London, we serve customers throughout the UK, North America, the EU, and APAC.

As we work towards €160m+ in annual revenue by 2027, we are seeking a Senior Google Ads Specialist to join us as soon as possible. You will lead Google Ads performance for one of our portfolio brands, taking direct responsibility for revenue growth, advertising efficiency, and profitability.

About the opportunity:

You will be part of an international business operating multiple e-commerce brands, with substantial advertising investment across several markets. Working at this scale means your decisions will directly influence revenue and commercial results.

Google Ads already plays a significant role in our growth. We are looking for someone who enjoys navigating international e-commerce, working with large datasets, and uncovering opportunities that deliver measurable improvements.

Working alongside our Head of Performance Marketing, creative team, and data specialists, you will use analysis, experimentation, and hands-on optimisation to develop this established channel further. Your focus will be on maintaining strong current performance while supporting efficient growth over time.

What you will be responsible for:

  • Own Google Ads performance across international markets for one of our e-commerce brands

  • Run and optimise Search, Shopping, Performance Max, and other relevant campaign formats

  • Monitor and improve core performance measures, including ROAS, CPA, conversion rate, revenue, and profitability

  • Drive growth and improve advertising efficiency across your assigned portfolio

  • Uncover opportunities within product ranges, categories, markets, and audience groups

  • Turn campaign insights into clear recommendations and practical next steps

  • Conduct account reviews and introduce continuous performance improvements

  • Work with developers and analytics colleagues to maintain accurate tracking and reliable measurement

  • Collaborate with creative and content teams to strengthen advertising effectiveness and landing page results

  • Contribute to budget allocation, forecasting, and performance reporting

  • Stay informed about platform updates, AI-powered advertising capabilities, and industry best practices

  • Help develop structured tests and experiments that strengthen account performance over time

The impact you can make:

Our Google Ads campaigns already generate results. You will build on that foundation by uncovering further opportunities, improving efficiency, and scaling successful approaches.

In a competitive e-commerce environment, even small improvements can make a significant commercial difference. You will connect campaign decisions to business outcomes and remain accountable for their impact.

You will collaborate with experienced colleagues who work quickly and place a high value on execution. We welcome independent judgment, evidence-based decisions, and constructive questions about existing approaches. You will have the trust to make decisions and directly support the company’s growth.



In-house e-commerce experience is a requirement for this position. Candidates whose Google Ads experience is primarily gained through agencies, consultancy, or freelance work will not be considered.

We are looking for someone who has owned performance within an e-commerce company, with results evaluated through revenue, profitability, customer acquisition, and sustained growth.

You should understand how campaign performance connects to wider commercial goals and be comfortable taking responsibility for both decision-making and implementation.

What you will bring:

  • A minimum of 2 years of practical experience managing Google Ads campaigns

  • A proven record of managing Google Ads within an e-commerce business, with direct accountability for results and profitability

  • Extensive practical knowledge of Search, Shopping, and Performance Max campaigns

  • Experience working as part of an in-house e-commerce team

  • The ability to analyse large datasets and identify opportunities that can be put into practice

  • A solid grasp of attribution, tracking, and performance measurement

  • Working familiarity with Google Analytics 4, Google Tag Manager, and Google Merchant Center

  • Strong analytical skills and a thorough approach to detail

  • Fluency in spoken and written English

  • The ability to adapt to shifting priorities in a fast-paced environment

  • A curious, proactive approach and a commitment to ongoing improvement

  • Confidence operating independently, making decisions, and owning the results

  • A readiness to use AI and automation as we continue introducing them across the business

  • Availability to start immediately or as soon as possible

Your working style:

You bring senior-level judgment while staying actively involved in campaign execution and performance. You draw clear conclusions from data and translate those findings into practical action.

You want to understand what drives results and regularly look for ways to improve them. You can move comfortably between longer-term planning and daily optimisation while keeping business growth and commercial outcomes in focus.

You enjoy developing and scaling campaigns, accepting responsibility for their performance, and helping an established channel continue to grow.

International collaboration and travel:

Our team works across London, Belgrade, Barcelona, Frankfurt, Oxfordshire, Istanbul, and Guangzhou. As the company grows, we are continuing to invest in our team presence.

The role includes travel approximately every 4–8 weeks to Belgrade, Barcelona, London, or other team locations. These visits provide time for joint planning, workshops, team gatherings, and strategic discussions.

Most work takes place remotely, complemented by regular opportunities to collaborate and plan together in person as the business scales.

This is a long-term opportunity to make a meaningful contribution to the growth of an international e-commerce group.

Our culture at ennovationHUB:

We value:

  • Taking ownership and following through on commitments

  • Turning plans into action

  • Communicating clearly and directly

  • Building knowledge through hands-on experience

We welcome people from different backgrounds who care about the quality of their work, take responsibility for their contribution, and help the business progress.

jobs.title: Marketing & Communications Manager (m/w/d)
jobs.description:
Du möchtest nicht einfach Marketing machen. Du möchtest etwas bewegen.

Du hast Freude daran, Dinge aufzubauen, Menschen zusammenzubringen und aus guten Ideen etwas Konkretes zu machen? Du bist neugierig, stellst Fragen und probierst auch mal neue Wege aus? Und Du findest, dass gute Ergebnisse am besten gemeinsam entstehen?

Dann könnten wir gut zusammenpassen.

Wir suchen keinen Menschen, der einfach nur einen Marketingplan abarbeitet. Wir suchen jemanden, der mitdenkt, Verantwortung übernimmt, Dinge hinterfragt und Lust hat, mit uns etwas zu gestalten.

Dabei glauben wir an klare Worte, gegenseitiges Vertrauen und hohe Ansprüche an unsere Arbeit. Wir nehmen unsere Aufgaben ernst – uns selbst aber nicht immer. Und wir sind überzeugt, dass Professionalität und Menschlichkeit zusammengehören.

Über OIXIO

OIXIO gehört zu den führenden IT-Anbietern Estlands – einem Land, das wie kaum ein anderes in Europa für gelebte Digitalisierung und einen hohen Stellenwert von Cybersecurity steht.

Was dort über viele Jahre gewachsen ist, bringen wir jetzt verstärkt nach Deutschland: technologische Kompetenz, pragmatische Lösungen, direkte Zusammenarbeit und die Überzeugung, dass gute Digitalisierung vor allem eines tun muss – funktionieren.

Mit OIXIO erminas verbinden wir diesen estnischen Spirit mit unserer langjährigen Erfahrung mit deutschen Hidden Champions im Mittelstand und unserer lokalen Basis in Oldenburg. Gemeinsam unterstützen wir Unternehmen dabei, ihre IT sicher, verlässlich und zukunftsfähig aufzustellen – von Cybersecurity und IT-Infrastruktur über Business-Anwendungen und Cloud bis zu Daten, KI und Industrial IoT.

In Deutschland stehen wir mit unserer gemeinsamen Geschichte noch am Anfang – und kaum jemand kennt hier bisher unseren Namen. Genau deshalb suchen wir jemanden, der das ändern will und lieber etwas aufbaut, als eine fertige Rolle zu übernehmen.

Die Aufgabe

Als Marketing & Communications Manager Deutschland machst Du OIXIO bei mittelständischen Industrieunternehmen bekannt und vertrauenswürdig – vor allem in Norddeutschland und Nordrhein-Westfalen – und schaffst die Gespräche, auf denen unser Vertrieb aufbaut.

Du entwickelst unsere Botschaften für den deutschen Markt und übersetzt unser Angebot in klare Geschichten für IT, Produktion und Geschäftsführung.

Gemeinsam mit unserem Sales Account Manager steuerst Du gezielte Kampagnen für eine definierte Liste von Zielunternehmen und machst aus Interesse konkrete Gespräche.

Du baust die Präsenz von OIXIO auf LinkedIn auf – für das Unternehmen sowie für unsere Expertinnen, Experten und Geschäftsführung.

Du pflegst Kontakte zu Fach- und Regionalmedien und platzierst Artikel, Fachbeiträge und Kundengeschichten.

Du organisierst eigene Veranstaltungen – vom Kundenfrühstück im Werk über Webinare bis zu Roundtables – und wählst die Messen und Netzwerkveranstaltungen aus, auf denen wir präsent sind.

Du erstellst Inhalte, die überzeugen: Case Studies, One-Pager, Präsentationen, Videos und Webinhalte – gemeinsam mit unseren Fachleuten in Deutschland, Estland und Litauen.

Du misst, was wirkt – Website-Besuche, Anfragen, Veranstaltungsteilnahmen, aktivierte Zielunternehmen und Vertriebstermine – und steuerst Deine Aktivitäten in Microsoft Dynamics 365 CRM.

Unsere Themen: Cybersecurity, Informationssicherheit, Managed IT Services, Microsoft Business Central/NAV-Modernisierung, Prozessdigitalisierung, Industrial IoT, Cloud, Daten und KI.

Was Du mitbringen solltest

  • Mehrjährige Erfahrung im B2B-Marketing oder in der Unternehmenskommunikation, idealerweise mit IT-Services, Managed Services, Industrieautomation, Beratung oder Business-Anwendungen.

  • Nachweisbare Erfolge darin, Sichtbarkeit aufzubauen und Nachfrage zu erzeugen – gerne auch als erste oder einzige Marketingverantwortliche in einem Unternehmen oder Markt.

  • Erfahrung mit Kampagnen für konkrete Zielunternehmen und mehrere Entscheiderinnen und Entscheider auf Kundenseite.

  • Gutes Verständnis für mittelständische Unternehmen, besonders im industriellen Umfeld, und die Fähigkeit, technische Themen verständlich zu erklären.

  • Starke Schreibkompetenz, sicherer Umgang mit LinkedIn, CRM und Web-Analytics, sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse und sehr gutes Englisch.

  • Du kennst die wichtigsten Werkzeuge des modernen B2B-Marketings und weißt, wie Du ihre Wirkung misst. Ob Dynamics 365, LinkedIn Campaign Manager, Analytics, SEO-Tools oder KI: Entscheidend ist für uns nicht, dass Du jedes Tool bereits beherrschst, sondern dass Du weißt, was Du erreichen willst, und Dich schnell in neue Werkzeuge einarbeiten kannst.

  • Flexibler Wohnort in Norddeutschland, sofern regelmäßige persönliche Treffen mit dem Team in unserem Büro in Oldenburg gut möglich sind; Reisebereitschaft deutschlandweit, gelegentlich auch nach Estland und Litauen.

Was gut zu uns passt

  • Du hast Freude daran, Dinge aufzubauen. Ein komplett bestelltes Feld brauchst Du nicht – im Gegenteil: Du erkennst Möglichkeiten, entwickelst Ideen und übernimmst Verantwortung dafür, daraus etwas zu machen.

  • Du bist neugierig auf Menschen, Unternehmen und Technologien und willst verstehen, bevor Du kommunizierst.

  • Du schätzt Flexibilität, möchtest aber nicht ausschließlich im Homeoffice arbeiten. Der persönliche Austausch im Team, mit unseren Kunden und mit der Presse ist Dir wichtig.

  • Du kannst die Stärke und Erfahrung einer etablierten internationalen IT-Gruppe nutzen und gleichzeitig mit uns herausfinden, was davon für den deutschen Mittelstand wirklich relevant ist.

  • Du arbeitest eigenständig, aber nicht als Einzelkämpfer. Bei uns ist Marketing Teamsport: Gute Ergebnisse entstehen gemeinsam mit Vertrieb, Consultants, Technik und Geschäftsführung.

  • Du misst Deinen Erfolg at Gesprächen und Kunden – nicht an Likes – und versprichst nichts, was unser Team nicht halten kann.

  • Und Du hast Lust, ein Stück des OIXIO Spirits aus Estland nach Deutschland zu bringen – und ihm hier gemeinsam mit uns eine eigene Handschrift zu geben.

Was wir bieten

  • Eine konkrete Rolle beim Aufbau von OIXIO in Deutschland – mit Gestaltungsspielraum und kurzen Entscheidungswegen.

  • Ein echtes Budget für Veranstaltungen, Inhalte und Medienarbeit sowie Unterstützung durch Spezialisten, wo es nötig ist.

  • Erfahrene Fachleute in Deutschland, Estland und Litauen, die Inhalte, Demos und Vorträge beisteuern.

  • Ein breites Leistungsportfolio rund um IT, Cybersecurity, Digitalisierung, Business-Anwendungen und Industrial IoT – mit vielen Geschichten, die erzählt werden wollen.

  • Ein internationales Arbeitsumfeld mit estnischer Bodenständigkeit, direkter Kommunikation und pragmatischer Zusammenarbeit.

  • Wir erwarten viel und geben auch viel zurück: Vertrauen, Freiraum, faire Bedingungen und Menschen, auf die Du Dich verlassen kannst.

Warum diese Rolle interessant ist

Deutschland ist für OIXIO ein wichtiger Wachstumsmarkt. Mit unserer lokalen Basis in Oldenburg, einem erfahrenen Team und einem relevanten Angebot passen wir gut zu den Herausforderungen vieler mittelständischer Industrieunternehmen – jetzt muss es der Markt nur noch erfahren.

Wenn Du Erfahrung im B2B-Marketing mitbringst, Lust hast, eine Marke von Grund auf bekannt zu machen, und lieber mit einem guten Team als mit großen Schlagworten arbeitest, freuen wir uns auf das Gespräch mit Dir.

Kuro is building the AI foundation for construction. We're reimagining how construction professionals get work done and make decisions by leveraging AI to augment back-office workflows and make core data accessible. We are not pursuing marginal improvements, but a step change for construction.

After one year on the market, leading construction enterprises with a combined annual construction volume of >€40 billion use Kuro every day to automate workflows and make faster, better decisions. We are 15 people based in Berlin. You will join a group of technical ex-founders and builders who are ambitious and kind.

Learn more: Join Kuro - Berlin

What You'll Do

Set the technical direction

  • Own the architecture decisions for the platform, from document ingestion to the chat UI

  • Write and review RFCs. The technical roadmap for the next two to three quarters is yours.

  • Make the build-or-buy decisions: which models we use, and which retrieval and orchestration stack we build on.

  • Turn a vague customer request (“show me where the bid deviates from the BoQ”) into a scoped plan with the risks named.

Raise the bar for the team

  • Mentor engineers: Review their designs and their code.

  • Define the engineering standards. Find what slows the team down, in tooling or in the CI/CD pipeline, and fix it.

  • Interview and hire engineers.

  • You have no direct reports. You change decisions in product and in other teams with a written argument.

Build and own end-to-end (AI) features

  • Design and implement new features to solve a specific user problem, such as document versioning or our agentic Chat.

  • From concept to DB schema, to optimizing LLMs, to UI. Own the full development lifecycle of customer-facing features.

  • Manage evaluations and scoring, and perform error analysis on new and shipped AI features.

Build the platform that abstracts workflow building

  • Contribute to the workflow harness, decision-trace standard, and eval tooling so a new use case ships in ~1 month

  • Build reusable human review & approval surfaces where trust in AI output is earned

Work on the construction ontology & project graph

  • Help model and evolve canonical entities of our customers

  • Contribute to entity resolution across sources: recognizing the same requirement, position, or price across BoQs, contracts, drawings, and bids

  • Build features so answers are evidence-linked and auditable, and decisions flow back into the graph

Contribute to scalable data pipelines & integrations

  • Extend our multi-modal ingestion of unstructured documents - PDFs, scans, drawings, and 3D models - orchestrated and cost-efficient at scale

  • Build read/write integrations with customer systems (document management, ERP/AVA), so workflows complete work end-to-end

Projects you would be involved in

Current & Past projects

  • Project & document versioning guaranteeing data lineage in construction projects

jobs.title: Staff Engineer
jobs.description:
About Andercore

Andercore is the AI-native supplier of industrial materials and goods for energy and infrastructure. We execute trade and distribution end-to-end, on our own account, at the speed of compute - and we are becoming the supplier of record for the entire industry.

Industrial procurement is a €900B market in Europe alone and the largest manual market on earth. 95% of customers have no direct access to global supply chains. Materials pass through four or five intermediaries before they reach a site, and 40% of the margin evaporates on the way. For decades, the operating system of this industry was people: people to source, negotiate, finance, ship, and sell.

We built the alternative from scratch. We are the supplier. We buy from global sources and sell to European customers on our own account. Our AI runs the full trade: sourcing, quality, pricing, sales, logistics, credit, and financing. One request. A firm quote in minutes. Delivered on time. For the customer, it feels like buying from their preferred local supplier. No warehouses. No fleet. No inventory risk. Every trade is pre-sold before it is bought.

We are also the credit counterparty. Customers are scored and insured in minutes and get up to 60 days of payment terms priced into the quote itself. The working capital behind every trade is bank-funded, not equity-funded.

Where we are today:

  • Strong triple-digit-million euro turnover run rate, the majority of it from repeat customers

  • Seven European markets live, sourced from suppliers across Asia and beyond

  • 80+ people across Berlin (HQ), London, and Shanghai

  • $90M raised in equity and debt, including our $40M Series B, from Atomico, Project A, Target Global, and Inven Capital - with working capital facilities from UniCredit and KfW

The margin is in the bits. The moat is in the atoms. We are building the supplier of record for industrial materials - and redefining how global trade works in one of the largest and most essential industries on earth.

About the role

Andercore runs global trade end to end, from sourcing and pricing to sales, logistics and financing, and AI agents do a growing share of that work. Order values are high and prices and stock change daily, so the systems underneath have to be fast, correct and reliable at all times.

As a Staff Engineer, you own our hardest technical problems and set the architecture across teams. You focus on what a fast-growing trading business cannot afford to get wrong: speed, reliability, security and observability. You report to our VP Engineering and work closely with our Senior Product Engineers, QA and product managers. You stay hands-on: you write code, review designs and raise the bar for everyone around you

Tech stack

Java 21 and Spring Boot 3, Python, LangGraph and LLM APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini), PostgreSQL, Kinesis, AWS with Terraform, GitHub Actions, and TypeScript with Node.js, Next.js and React. Including Salesforce, which we are moving our transaction core out of.

 

What you will do

  • Set the technical direction across teams: define the target architecture, write the RFCs behind big decisions, and make sure teams build towards the same picture.

  • Lead the hardest technical work yourself, from design to production, instead of only advising on it.

  • Shape the carve-out of our transaction core from Salesforce into a modern, modular core system, with a migration path that never disrupts daily trading.

  • Make reliability, security and observability part of how we build: monitoring, alerting, incident response and postmortems that lead to real changes.

  • Design how our AI agents act safely on money-touching paths, with evaluations, guardrails, audit trails and human review where it matters.

  • Set standards for correctness and data integrity, including idempotency, validation and testing, together with QA.

  • Mentor engineers through design reviews, pairing and direct feedback, and help us hire by defining what great engineering looks like at Andercore.

 

In your first six months, you might

  • Design the architecture of our pricing engine so it scales with a growing assortment and more markets, and serves correct prices to sales, and later directly to customers, in milliseconds.

  • Lay out the target architecture and first steps for moving our transaction core off Salesforce.

  • Build the observability and incident setup that lets us catch problems before customers or colleagues notice them

     

What you bring

  • At least 8 years of experience building and running software in production, including systems where errors cost real money.

  • Deep backend expertise at production scale in Java or a comparable language such as Kotlin, C# or Go, and willingness to work in Java and Spring Boot.

  • A track record of setting architecture across several teams, through influence rather than a management title.

  • Experience designing transactional, distributed and event-driven systems, with a strong focus on correctness, failure modes and performance.

  • Hands-on depth in reliability, security and observability, and experience leading incidents and postmortems.

  • Experience in a fast-growing company, and a track record of solving business problems, not only technical ones.

  • AI is part of your daily work. Experience building or evaluating AI agents in production is a strong plus.

  • Experience with re-platforming or carving out systems from a platform like Salesforce or an ERP is a plus

 

Practical details

  • Location: Berlin, hybrid

  • Working language: English

  • A learning budget for your development

  • Start date: As soon as possible

We are an equal-opportunity employer and welcome applicants from all backgrounds, regardless of race, ethnicity, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, religion, age, disability, or any other characteristic. We believe that diversity drives innovation, creativity, and collective strength.

jobs.title: Field Service Engineer – Semiconductor Equipment (f/m/d)
jobs.description:
Description

Our quantum sensing technology is already operating in customer environments across Taiwan, the United States, and Europe. As our installed base grows and we move from first deployments to repeat orders, ensuring the reliability and performance of every system becomes increasingly important.

As our Field Service Engineer, you'll take hands-on ownership of our systems throughout their operational lifecycle — from installation and commissioning to preventive maintenance, troubleshooting, and repair.

You'll work directly with leading semiconductor foundries, IDMs, and OSATs, ensuring our systems operate reliably and consistently meet their specifications. You'll collaborate closely with our Engineering and Applications teams, combining technical problem-solving with a strong customer focus.

This is also an opportunity to help shape our global service function from an early stage, introducing the processes, tools, and standards that will support our growing international installed base.

Who we are

Founded in 2022 as a spin-off of TU Munich, QD leverages quantum sensors to rapidly capture three-dimensional current maps within multi-layer chips. Our strong, international team of over 70, including physicists, engineers, data scientists, and other experts, works side by side with major semiconductor manufacturers, supporting chip debugging and accelerating yield analysis. Backed by top-tier deep tech investors, semiconductor experts, and strategic public programs, we have ensured long-term stability, shifting from breakthrough to scale - and shaping the next chapter in chip testing.

Why join Quantum Diamonds?

jobs.title: AI Builder — Working Student
jobs.description:
EggAI Labs · Working Student · In Person (Tübingen, Germany)

Designing lifecycle evaluation for nondeterministic domain-specific AI systems.

EggAI Labs

We're opening the EggAI Labs in Tübingen. The Labs purpose is to test new AI capabilities, identify what works, how they'd improve delivery, and then build assets to support teams and clients. EggAI's mission cannot be achieved through one-off client projects alone and the Labs is the way to adapt and scale.

As part of the first cohort, you will join a small peer group and work directly with EggAI's CAIO, a Tübingen alumnus. You will also collaborate with our engineering, product, and project leads, who will bring you insights from client problems, help you understand their context and challenge your solutions for them. Your fellow AI Builders will be deliberately chosen to span different passions and strenghts. You will have room to explore and be expected to turn that exploration into something useful. This is not a client-facing role.

The problem: EvalOps

How do we prove an AI system acts as expected under various conditions?

We will explore EvalOps: the methods and tools used to check whether domain-specific AI systems meet their behavioral requirements. Among the key challenges for operating AI systems are nondeterminism, ground-truth curation, evaluation metric-design, latency and costs. EvalOps need to overcome all of them in a disciplined way.

These questions will guide the initial work:

  • Regression suites: How can domain experts turn traces, code, and prompts into useful evals in a way that scales?

  • Coverage estimation: How can we quantify the gaps between an eval suite and the range of expected agent behaviors?

  • Live monitoring: Is it possible to detect anomalous behaviour in production with a similar precision to regression evals?

  • Eval analysis: How much evidence is enough to act (e.g., deploy, debug, roll back a feature, choose a different model)? You will help refine them, test approaches, create assets, and pose new questions.

The role

As an AI Builder, you will take an open EvalOps problem from investigation to a working prototype, ready to be tested. Whatever your focus, you will be expected to take a problem through to a useful result. Here is what that means in practice:

  • Research emerging AI and evaluation capabilities and distinguish substance from hype.

  • Understand the user, workflow, domain, and organisational problem around the work.

  • Evaluate usefulness, quality, safety, and reliability with appropriate evidence.

  • Communicate decisions and learning clearly.

  • Create assets that other people can understand, use, and improve.

  • Code and build end to end.

This shared foundation leaves room for different strengths and interests. Each AI Builder will then develop greater depth in one of three pillars.

Three pillars, different passions

Pillar

Driving question

Possible EvalOps focus

Product

What should we build?

Workflows and interfaces that help domain experts create evals, inspect traces, understand results, and make decisions.

Engineering

How should we build it?

Dependable and scalable evaluation infrastructure, trace processing, monitoring, and governance tooling.

Data Science

How do we know it works?

Coverage measures, sampling strategies, scoring methods, statistical tests, anomaly detection, and reasoning under uncertainty.

We expect every AI Builder to develop a practical foundation across all three pillars and to pursue greater depth in the one that most strongly matches their passion.

What we value

  • Problem obsession. A difficult question captures your curiosity. You keep returning to it, pursue ideas without waiting for instructions, and care deeply about finding an answer that works.

  • Initiative and follow-through. You turn uncertainty into something you can investigate, test, and improve—and stay resourceful when the first approach fails.

  • Evidence of making things work. Show us something you created, the decisions you made, and what you learned along the way.

  • Independent judgment. You test new capabilities yourself, distinguish evidence from enthusiasm, and change your mind when the findings warrant it.

  • Generosity in collaboration. You explain your thinking, seek candid feedback, act on it, and help others make progress. 

What is required

  • You are pursuing a Master’s degree.

  • You can write code and turn an idea into working, tested software.

  • You can work from Tübingen and communicate fluently in English, our company language.

Relevant fields include Computer Science, Machine Learning, Mathematics, Physics, Bioinformatics, Computational Neuroscience, Medical Informatics, Quantitative Data Science, Cognitive Science. We also welcome candidates from other disciplines who can demonstrate strong problem-solving and practical technical ability.

What you will gain

  • Industry insight. Learn what works and what breaks in real enterprise AI systems, with access to problems from EggAI’s client work

  • Meaningful ownership. Take an EvalOps problem from investigation to a working, evaluated solution, with freedom to shape the approach.

  • Close mentorship. Work directly with EggAI’s Chief AI Officer and sharpen your judgment through feedback from engineering, product, and project leads.

  • Room to develop. Deepen your strengths, learn from peers with complementary perspectives, and use modern AI-development tools on unresolved problems.

  • A say in the Lab’s direction. Help establish its working practices, propose new questions, and influence what it pursues next.

  • Competitive compensation, including recognition for exceptional contributions, and a potential path to a full-time EggAI role after graduation.

How to apply

A short cover letter is required.

Your CV tells us what you have done so far, but we're also interested in the why. Use the letter to explain why you made those choices, what drives you, and why the AI Builder role at EggAI Labs feels like the right next step in your career. 

We are looking for exceptional students, and excellence takes many forms, e.g., academic results, research or ambitious projects. Whatever form yours takes, show us the appropriate evidence, be it grades, publications, something you've built or other evidence of impact.

This is an in-person role in Tübingen. We can only consider candidates who live within commuting distance.

jobs.description:
Adaptyv is building an automated lab that lets AI agents run biology experiments.

We're entering the era of agentic science where AI models can now design novel proteins, propose hypotheses, and iterate on experimental results. But they can't run the experiments themselves - that's still a manual, months-long process. We're building the infrastructure that gives AI agents access to the physical world.

We are one of the fastest growing biotech companies, trusted by leading biopharmas, frontier AI labs, and the techbio companies pushing the field forward. This is a rare chance to help advance some of the most important work happening in biotech today.

Our automated lab is powered by a deep software + hardware stack: lab instruments worth millions of USD reverse-engineered into API-controllable hardware, dozens of devices orchestrated through complex workflows, full observability on everything that happens in the lab, processing pipelines for messy physical-world data, and AI systems that troubleshoot production results and accelerate assay development.

We’re growing rapidly and are hiring for talented people to scale and support the massive demand for AI-driven wet lab experimentation.

About the role

This is a hybrid sales and customer success role for someone with real scientific depth. You'll be the primary point of contact for customers — from first conversation through ongoing engagement. That means understanding what a protein design team is actually trying to achieve, helping them pick the right assays, making sure their experiments are set up correctly, and translating results back into language that's useful for their programs.

The day-to-day:

  • Running technical sales calls where you discuss binding kinetics, expression systems, and assay design, not just pricing

  • Onboarding new customers and helping them design their first experiments on the platform

  • Monitoring ongoing accounts, flagging issues early, and proactively suggesting next steps based on their results

  • Working with the biology team to troubleshoot when a customer's experiment doesn't go as expected

  • Identifying expansion opportunities within existing accounts — new targets, new assay types, larger campaigns

You won't be handed a script. You'll need to understand the science well enough to earn trust from PhD-level protein engineers and CSOs, while also being commercially sharp enough to close deals and grow accounts.

Responsibilities

  • Own the full customer lifecycle: prospecting, technical sales conversations, deal closing, onboarding, and ongoing account management.

  • Serve as the technical point of contact for customers. Understand their protein engineering goals and recommend the right experiments (binding, expression, thermostability, enzyme activity).

  • Understand and explain our assay capabilities in depth: BLI, SPR, cell-free expression, and emerging assay types. Know when each is appropriate and what the data means.

  • Work closely with the biology team to ensure experiments are designed correctly and results are communicated clearly.

  • Build and maintain a pipeline of commercial opportunities across customer segments: AI-driven protein design companies, biotech startups, pharma R&D teams, and academic labs.

  • Develop proposals and quotes tailored to customer needs, from small pilot experiments to large-scale data generation campaigns.

  • Represent Adaptyv at conferences and industry events. Be able to have deep technical conversations at the booth, not just hand out brochures.

  • Feed customer insights back to the product and biology teams: what assays are people asking for, what's missing, where are we losing deals.

What we're looking for

  • Scientific background in protein engineering, biochemistry, biophysics, or a related field. You should be comfortable discussing binding kinetics (KD, kon, koff), expression systems, and assay design without needing to look things up.

  • Experience in a customer-facing technical role: field application scientist, technical sales, scientific account management, or similar. CRO or biotech vendor experience is a strong plus.

  • Strong communicator who can adapt to the audience: detailed and technical with a scientist, concise and business-focused with a VP.

  • Self-starter who can manage their own pipeline and priorities without heavy oversight.

  • Genuine interest in AI-driven protein design and the companies working in this space. You follow what's happening in the field.

Adaptyv is building an automated lab that lets AI agents run biology experiments.

We're entering the era of agentic science where AI models can now design novel proteins, propose hypotheses, and iterate on experimental results. But they can't run the experiments themselves - that's still a manual, months-long process. We're building the infrastructure that gives AI agents access to the physical world.

We are one of the fastest growing biotech companies, trusted by leading biopharmas, frontier AI labs, and the techbio companies pushing the field forward. This is a rare chance to help advance some of the most important work happening in biotech today.

Our automated lab is powered by a deep software + hardware stack: lab instruments worth millions of USD reverse-engineered into API-controllable hardware, dozens of devices orchestrated through complex workflows, full observability on everything that happens in the lab, processing pipelines for messy physical-world data, and AI systems that troubleshoot production results and accelerate assay development.

We’re growing rapidly and are hiring for talented people to scale and support the massive demand for AI-driven wet lab experimentation.

About the Role

You'll build work-cell orchestration, instrument drivers, protocol scheduling, error-recovery logic, and monitoring. Physical systems fail in ways pure software doesn't — a plate gets stuck, a liquid handler skips a well, a temperature controller drifts. Your job is to make the system handle all of it gracefully. This is a broad, hands-on role for a strong engineer who wants their code to drive real machines and see it run the same day.

What You'll Do

  • Build orchestration software that coordinates liquid handlers, plate readers, incubators, and robot arms — handling timing dependencies, state, and error recovery.

  • Reverse-engineer and develop instrument drivers and APIs. Each instrument speaks a different protocol (serial, USB, TCP/IP); you work out how it talks and build a clean abstraction over it.

  • Model and execute complex multi-step protocols reliably — a single run can span dozens of steps across multiple instruments.

  • Build error-recovery logic so that when something fails mid-run, the system retries, skips, alerts, or pauses depending on the failure mode.

  • Create monitoring and observability for work-cell health: instrument status, run progress, error rates.

  • Debug across the software–hardware boundary — figuring out whether bad data is a comms, firmware, calibration, or code problem.

  • Work closely with lab automation engineers, the rest of the software team, and the scientists running production.

Stack

TypeScript and Python, Postgres (Supabase), Modal for compute. We control instruments with open-source Python tooling like PyLabRobot and PyHamilton wherever we can, rather than proprietary vendor GUIs.

What We're Looking For

  • Strong software engineering skills. You write production code in Python and/or TypeScript — well-structured and maintainable, not just prototypes.

About the Role

Our lab produces binding data faster than any one person can look at it. Runs come off the Gators and the Carterra, go through our processing pipeline, and land in a review queue. Somebody with real judgment then has to decide: is this curve real? Is that a fit artifact or a genuine two-state binding event? Does this replicate get delivered, or does the sample get re-run? That person is you.

The second half of the job is talking to the customer about it. When a design team gets a plate back and three of their best predictions look like non-binders, they want to talk to someone who can explain why: reference subtraction, avidity, an off-rate at the edge of what the instrument resolves, or simply a bad protein. You'll be that person, on the call, sharing your screen, walking through sensorgrams.

This is a role for a scientist who is very good at kinetics and also likes people. If you like one but not the other, you'll be unhappy here.

What You'll Do

  • Review the binding data coming out of the lab. Every SPR and BLI run passes through our processing pipeline and then to human review, and you're the expert eye on the output. You decide what gets delivered, what gets flagged, and what gets re-run.

  • Judge the curves, not just the numbers. A clean-looking Kd on a bad fit is worse than no number at all. You know the difference between a real off-rate and a drifting baseline, and you can say why.

  • Review data from our other assays too: thermostability, expression, developability, enzyme activity. Binding is the core of the role but it isn't all of it.

  • Talk to customers about their results. Deliverable walkthroughs, follow-up questions, and the awkward conversation when the data doesn't say what they hoped. You explain what we measured, how confident we are, and what to do next.

  • Turn review into experimental design. When something needs a re-run, you decide what changes: orientation, regeneration, concentration series, or a switch from BLI to SPR for the sensitivity.

  • Analyze at the batch level, not just the sample level. With hundreds of results per experiment, you should be writing a script to find the pattern rather than clicking through a queue. Systematic drift, a bad reference channel, or a target lot behaving differently than the last one shows up in aggregate long before it shows up in any single curve.

  • Feed what you learn back into the pipeline. When you catch a case where automation passed something it shouldn't have, or failed something it shouldn't have, that becomes a concrete requirement for the software team.

  • Work closely with production (what actually happened in the lab), QC (systematic quality), and customer success (the relationship around the science).

  • Deep SPR and BLI experience. Biacore, Carterra, Octet, Gator: the platform matters less than the fact that you've run these assays, troubleshot them, and interpreted a lot of data from them. You've seen enough sensorgrams to know immediately when one is lying to you.

  • Real fitting judgment. 1:1 vs. bivalent, when steady-state is appropriate and when it isn't, how mass transport and avidity distort a result. You can defend a Kd, or refuse to report one.

  • Strong data analysis skills. Python or R, enough to pull a few hundred results out of a database, fit them, plot them, and find the outliers. This role generates too much data to review by hand.

  • You use AI tools seriously. We’re growing rapidly and are hiring for talented people to scale and support the massive demand for AI-driven wet lab experimentation.

About the Role

Our lab is a factory. DNA goes in, characterized proteins come out, and a customer gets results in days rather than the months a CRO would take. Everything that machine consumes — synthesized genes, reagents, consumables, biosensors, catalog proteins — is something we buy, on lead times we do not control. It is also most of what a protein costs to make, which makes procurement one of the biggest levers on gross margin in the business.

So far scientists have bought what they need, decisions get made in hours, and nothing blocks an experiment. That was the right trade while we were proving the thing works. But we are multiplying lab throughput several times over, and at that volume procurement becomes a discipline: real terms with the suppliers we already buy from heavily, qualified second sources where we currently have one, inventory that is planned rather than remembered. Nobody has taken that on yet.

You would be our first dedicated supply chain hire, and it is hands-on — you do the sourcing and the negotiating yourself. One thing makes it harder than a typical procurement job: our assay portfolio keeps expanding, and every new assay brings new reagents. You are not optimizing a static supply chain, you are building one that flexes with the science. How far the role goes from there is up to you.

What You'll Do

  • Own procurement end to end. Every input to the lab, from gene synthesis down to gloves. Requests, POs, receiving, vendor onboarding, the lot.

  • De-risk the supply chain. Too much of what we depend on has exactly one supplier. Find second sources, qualify them properly with the science team, and keep them warm, so that switching is a decision we make rather than an emergency we react to.

  • Negotiate. Build the supplier relationships across our DNA, reagent, biosensor and catalog-protein vendors, put volume commitments and pricing agreements in place, and go get the margin back.

  • Drive down the cost of a protein. Go category by category and take cost out of each. A few francs per protein, multiplied across the volumes we are heading toward, is a seven-figure line.

  • Stay ahead of the science. When R&D says they are adding a new assay next quarter, you should already be sourcing the reagents for it.

  • Set inventory policy, and make the numbers true. Reorder points and safety stock, so we never stall a customer experiment on a stockout and never have six figures of reagents quietly expiring in a freezer. You decide what should be on the shelves and how much of it.

  • Plan supply for the lab expansion. Model what several-fold throughput actually needs — volumes, lead times, storage, cash tied up in stock — and have it in place before the capacity comes online, not after.

  • Own landed cost. Shipping, customs, import duties, VAT recoverability, cold chain. We import a lot of biology into Switzerland and both the cost and the failure modes matter.

  • Own COGS with Finance. Procurement and finance are the two halves of gross margin, and you are the procurement half.

  • Automate the whole thing. Ordering, tracking, and reconciliation should mostly run themselves.

What We're Looking For

  • You have worked in supply chain or procurement in a physical, technical business. Biotech, a CRO, or another life science company is ideal, and you understand reagent categories — enzymes, antibodies, media, resins, plasticware — and how they are actually sourced. Hardware manufacturing or another high-mix production setting translates well. Buying software licences does not. You do not need to have run a supply chain organization before; you do need to be ready to own one.

  • You think in margins. Saving a few francs per protein across tens of thousands of proteins a month is a number that should make you sit up.

  • You are technical enough to talk to scientists. You do not need a degree in biology, but you will be qualifying an alternative supplier for a reagent that a protein biochemist depends on, and you need to be able to have that conversation properly rather than forwarding it.

  • You can negotiate. Comfortable sitting across from vendors who have been selling into labs for thirty years, and comfortable walking away.

  • You automate. We run on Claude Code across the company and our lab system has an API. Some of our largest suppliers still require a human to upload a spreadsheet to a portal, and we consider that a bug rather than a fact of life. The best version of this person is writing scripts against our systems and our vendors' systems, not clicking through them. If your instinct is that procurement is a portal-and-email job, we will frustrate each other.

  • Obsessive about the details that bite. Lead times, expiry dates, lot numbers, minimum order quantities. Nothing falls through.

  • You want to grow fast. We are going from roughly 25 people to roughly 50 in the next year, and the lab spend grows faster than the headcount does.

  • Swiss or EU import/export experience is a strong plus.

Scope

We are a small company and nobody here has clean edges around their job. You will end up in the lab, in a spreadsheet with Finance, on the phone with a courier, and every so often doing something that is nobody's job simply because it needs doing. That is the deal, and if it sounds unappealing then we are probably not the right place.

What we do want to be clear about is where the centre of gravity is. This role is about what we buy, who we buy it from, what we pay, and how reliably it turns up. Sourcing, negotiation, supplier relationships, inventory, resilience, cost. Plenty of other things will land on your desk and you should take them, but that is the part that is yours and the part we will judge the role on.

One thing it is not: an order-taking job. You are not a mailbox between scientists and vendors. You decide what we source and from whom, and we expect you to argue with us about it.

Why This Role Is Interesting

Most supply chain jobs are about keeping a stable system stable. This one is about building the supply chain for a lab that is about to grow several-fold, at a company where the cost and reliability of an experiment more or less is the product. Every franc you take out of the cost of a protein, and every week you take out of a lead time, shows up directly in what we can offer customers and in whether AI-designed biology is cheap enough to be worth doing at scale. There are not many procurement jobs where the leverage is that direct, or that visible to the people running the company.
